sanskrit_iast:
bahiṣprajño vibhur viśvo hy antaḥprajñas tu taijasaḥ
ghanaprajñas tathā prājña eka eva tridhā smṛtaḥ //
meaning:
बहिष्प्रज्ञो विभुर् विश्वो ह्य् अन्तःप्रज्ञस् तु तैजसः
घनप्रज्ञस् तथा प्राज्ञ एक एव त्रिधा स्मृतः //
text_mt:
Viśva, the all-pervading, is conscious of the external; Taijasa is conscious of the internal;
and Prājña is a mass of consciousness: the one alone is regarded in three ways.
title: atha gauḍapādīya-kārikāḥ

sanskrit_iast:
dakṣiṇākṣimukhe viśvo manasy antas tu taijasaḥ
ākāśe ca hṛdi prājñas tridhā dehe vyavasthitaḥ //
meaning:
दक्षिणाक्षिमुखे विश्वो मनस्य् अन्तस् तु तैजसः
आकाशे च हृदि प्राज्ञस् त्रिधा देहे व्यवस्थितः //
text_mt:
Viśva is situated in the right eye as its face; Taijasa is within the mind;
and Prājña is in the space within the heart: threefold is he situated in the body.

sanskrit_iast:
viśvo hi sthūlabhuṅ nityaṃ taijasaḥ praviviktabhuk
ānandabhuk tathā prājñas tridhā bhogaṃ nibodhata //
meaning:
विश्वो हि स्थूलभुङ् नित्यं तैजसः प्रविविक्तभुक्
आनन्दभुक् तथा प्राज्ञस् त्रिधा भोगं निबोधत //
text_mt:
Viśva constantly enjoys the gross; Taijasa enjoys the subtle;
and Prājña enjoys bliss: understand the enjoyment to be threefold.

sanskrit_iast:
sthūlaṃ tarpayate viśvaṃ praviviktaṃ tu taijasam
ānandaś ca tathā prājñaṃ tridhā tṛptiṃ nibodhata //
meaning:
स्थूलं तर्पयते विश्वं प्रविविक्तं तु तैजसम्
आनन्दश् च तथा प्राज्ञं त्रिधा तृप्तिं निबोधत //
text_mt:
The gross satisfies Viśva, while the subtle [satisfies] Taijasa,
and bliss likewise [satisfies] Prājña: understand the satisfaction to be threefold.

sanskrit_iast:
triṣu dhāmasu yad bhojyaṃ bhoktā yaś ca prakīrtitaḥ
vedaitad ubhayaṃ yas tu sa bhuñjāno na lipyate //
meaning:
त्रिषु धामसु यद् भोज्यं भोक्ता यश् च प्रकीर्तितः
वेदैतद् उभयं यस् तु स भुञ्जानो न लिप्यते //
text_mt:
That which is to be enjoyed in the three realms and who is proclaimed as the enjoyer—
he who knows both of these is not tainted even while enjoying.

sanskrit_iast:
prabhavaḥ sarvabhāvānāṃ satām iti viniścayaḥ
sarvaṃ janayati prāṇaś cetoaṃśūn puruṣaḥ pṛthak //
meaning:
प्रभवः सर्वभावानां सताम् इति विनिश्चयः
सर्वं जनयति प्राणश् चेतोअंशून् पुरुषः पृथक् //
text_mt:
The settled conclusion is that [this is] the origination of existing entities;
Prāṇa generates everything, and Puruṣa produces the rays of consciousness separately.

sanskrit_iast:
vibhūtiṃ prasavaṃ tv anye manyante sṛṣṭicintakāḥ
svapnamāyāsarūpeti sṛṣṭir anyair vikalpitā //
meaning:
विभूतिं प्रसवं त्व् अन्ये मन्यन्ते सृष्टिचिन्तकाः
स्वप्नमायासरूपेति सृष्टिर् अन्यैर् विकल्पिता //
text_mt:
Other theorists of creation consider creation to be the manifestation of [divine] power;
by others creation is conceptually constructed as having the nature of a dream or an illusion.

sanskrit_iast:
icchāmātraṃ prabhoḥ sṛṣṭir iti sṛṣṭau viniścitāḥ
kālāt prasūtiṃ bhūtānāṃ manyante kālacintakāḥ //
meaning:
इच्छामात्रं प्रभोः सृष्टिर् इति सृष्टौ विनिश्चिताः
कालात् प्रसूतिं भूतानां मन्यन्ते कालचिन्तकाः //
text_mt:
Those resolved on [the theory of] creation [hold] that creation is merely the will of the Lord;
the theorists of time consider the birth of beings to be from time.

sanskrit_iast:
bhogārthaṃ sṛṣtir ity anye krīḍārtham iti cāpare
devasyaiṣa svabhāvo 'yam āptakāmasya kā spṛhā //
meaning:
भोगार्थं सृष्तिर् इत्य् अन्ये क्रीडार्थम् इति चापरे
देवस्यैष स्वभावो ऽयम् आप्तकामस्य का स्पृहा //
text_mt:
Others [say] creation is for the sake of enjoyment, and others that it is for the sake of play;
this is the own-nature of the deity: what desire can there be for one whose desires are fulfilled?

sanskrit_iast:
nivṛtteḥ sarvaduḥkhānām īśānaḥ prabhur avyayaḥ
advaitaḥ sarvabhāvānāṃ devas turyo vibhuḥ smṛtaḥ //
meaning:
निवृत्तेः सर्वदुःखानाम् ईशानः प्रभुर् अव्ययः
अद्वैतः सर्वभावानां देवस् तुर्यो विभुः स्मृतः //
text_mt:
The ruler, the Lord, the imperishable, [is responsible] for the cessation of all sufferings;
the non-dual among all entities, the deity is known as the fourth state, the all-pervading.

sanskrit_iast:
kāryakāraṇabaddhau tāv iṣyete viśvataijasau
prājñaḥ kāraṇabaddhas tu dvau tau turye na sidhyataḥ //
meaning:
कार्यकारणबद्धौ ताव् इष्येते विश्वतैजसौ
प्राज्ञः कारणबद्धस् तु द्वौ तौ तुर्ये न सिध्यतः //
text_mt:
Those two, Viśva and Taijasa, are held to be bound by cause and effect;
Prājña, however, is bound by cause; those two do not exist in the fourth state.

sanskrit_iast:
nātmānaṃ na parāṃś caiva na satyaṃ nāpi cānṛtam
prājñaḥ kiṃcana saṃvetti turyaṃ tat sarvadṛk sadā //
meaning:
नात्मानं न परांश् चैव न सत्यं नापि चानृतम्
प्राज्ञः किंचन संवेत्ति तुर्यं तत् सर्वदृक् सदा //
text_mt:
Prājña knows nothing at all—neither itself nor another,
neither truth nor untruth; the fourth state sees all, always.

sanskrit_iast:
dvaitasyāgrahaṇaṃ tulyam ubhayoḥ prājñaturyayoḥ
bījanidrāyutaḥ prājñaḥ sā ca turye na vidyate //
meaning:
द्वैतस्याग्रहणं तुल्यम् उभयोः प्राज्ञतुर्ययोः
बीजनिद्रायुतः प्राज्ञः सा च तुर्ये न विद्यते //
text_mt:
Non-apprehension of duality is common to both Prājña and the fourth state;
Prājña is associated with causal sleep, and that does not exist in the fourth state.

sanskrit_iast:
svapnanidrāyutāv ādyau prājñas tv asvapnanidrayā
na nidrāṃ naiva ca svapnaṃ turye paśyanti niścitāḥ //
meaning:
स्वप्ननिद्रायुताव् आद्यौ प्राज्ञस् त्व् अस्वप्ननिद्रया
न निद्रां नैव च स्वप्नं तुर्ये पश्यन्ति निश्चिताः //
text_mt:
The first two are associated with dream and sleep, but Prājña is [associated] with sleep devoid of dream;
those who are resolute see neither sleep nor dream in the fourth state.

sanskrit_iast:
anyathā gṛhṇataḥ svapno nidrā tattvam ajānataḥ
viparyāse tayoḥ kṣīṇe turīyaṃ padam aśnute //
meaning:
अन्यथा गृह्णतः स्वप्नो निद्रा तत्त्वम् अजानतः
विपर्यासे तयोः क्षीणे तुरीयं पदम् अश्नुते //
text_mt:
Dream belongs to one who apprehends falsely; sleep belongs to one who does not know reality;
when the error in those two is destroyed, one attains the fourth state.

sanskrit_iast:
anādimāyayā supto yadā jīvaḥ prabudhyate
ajam anidram asvapnam advaitaṃ budhyate tadā //
meaning:
अनादिमायया सुप्तो यदा जीवः प्रबुध्यते
अजम् अनिद्रम् अस्वप्नम् अद्वैतं बुध्यते तदा //
text_mt:
When the individual soul, asleep through beginningless illusion, awakens,
then it understands the unborn, sleepless, dreamless, non-dual [Self].

sanskrit_iast:
prapañco yadi vidyeta nivarteta na saṃśayaḥ
māyāmātram idaṃ dvaitam advaitaṃ paramārthataḥ //
meaning:
प्रपञ्चो यदि विद्येत निवर्तेत न संशयः
मायामात्रम् इदं द्वैतम् अद्वैतं परमार्थतः //
text_mt:
If the phenomenal manifestation did exist, it would cease, no doubt;
this duality is merely an illusion: non-dual in ultimate truth.

sanskrit_iast:
vikalpo vinivarteta kalpito yadi kenacit
upadeśād ayaṃ vādo jñāte dvaitaṃ na vidyate //
meaning:
विकल्पो विनिवर्तेत कल्पितो यदि केनचित्
उपदेशाद् अयं वादो ज्ञाते द्वैतं न विद्यते //
text_mt:
Conceptual construction would cease if it had been conceptually constructed by someone;
this teaching is for instruction; once known, duality does not exist.

sanskrit_iast:
viśvasyātvavivakṣāyām ādisāmānyam utkaṭam
mātrāsaṃpratipattau syād āptisāmānyam eva ca //
meaning:
विश्वस्यात्वविवक्षायाम् आदिसामान्यम् उत्कटम्
मात्रासंप्रतिपत्तौ स्याद् आप्तिसामान्यम् एव च //
text_mt:
In wishing to express the identity of Viśva with 'a', the commonality of being first is prominent;
and in realizing the mora, there is also the commonality of pervading.

sanskrit_iast:
taijasasyotvavijñāne utkarṣo dṛśyate sphuṭam
mātrāsaṃpratipattau syād ubhayatvaṃ tathāvidham //
meaning:
तैजसस्योत्वविज्ञाने उत्कर्षो दृश्यते स्फुटम्
मात्रासंप्रतिपत्तौ स्याद् उभयत्वं तथाविधम् //
text_mt:
In understanding the identity of Taijasa with 'u', superiority is clearly seen;
and in realizing the mora, there is being intermediate in the same way.

sanskrit_iast:
makārabhāve prājñasya mānasāmānyam utkaṭam
mātrāsaṃpratipattau tu layasāmānyam eva ca //
meaning:
मकारभावे प्राज्ञस्य मानसामान्यम् उत्कटम्
मात्रासंप्रतिपत्तौ तु लयसामान्यम् एव च //
text_mt:
In the identity of Prājña with the 'm'-sound, the commonality of measuring is prominent;
and in realizing the mora, there is also the commonality of dissolution.

sanskrit_iast:
triṣu dhāmasu yat tulyaṃ sāmānyaṃ vetti niścitaḥ
sa pūjyaḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ vandyaś caiva mahāmuniḥ //
meaning:
त्रिषु धामसु यत् तुल्यं सामान्यं वेत्ति निश्चितः
स पूज्यः सर्वभूतानां वन्द्यश् चैव महामुनिः //
text_mt:
He who resolutely knows what is equal, the common feature in the three realms,
is to be honored and praised by all beings, a great sage.

sanskrit_iast:
akāro nayate viśvam ukāraś cāpi taijasam
makāraś ca punaḥ prājñaṃ nāmātre vidyate gatiḥ //
meaning:
अकारो नयते विश्वम् उकारश् चापि तैजसम्
मकारश् च पुनः प्राज्ञं नामात्रे विद्यते गतिः //
text_mt:
The letter 'a' leads to Viśva, and the letter 'u' to Taijasa,
and the letter 'm' further to Prājña; in the measureless there is no going.

sanskrit_iast:
oṃkāraṃ pādaśo vidyāt pādā mātrā na saṃśayaḥ
oṃkāraṃ pādaśo jñātvā na kiṃcid api cintayet //
meaning:
ओंकारं पादशो विद्यात् पादा मात्रा न संशयः
ओंकारं पादशो ज्ञात्वा न किंचिद् अपि चिन्तयेत् //
text_mt:
One should know Omkāra quarter by quarter; the quarters are the morae, without doubt;
having known Omkāra quarter by quarter, one should not think of anything at all.

sanskrit_iast:
yuñjīta praṇave cetaḥ praṇavo brahma nirbhayam
praṇave nityayuktasya na bhayaṃ vidyate kvacit //
meaning:
युञ्जीत प्रणवे चेतः प्रणवो ब्रह्म निर्भयम्
प्रणवे नित्ययुक्तस्य न भयं विद्यते क्वचित् //
text_mt:
One should fix the mind on Praṇava; Praṇava is Brahman, fearless;
for one who is constantly joined to Praṇava, there is no fear anywhere.

sanskrit_iast:
praṇavo hy aparaṃ brahma praṇavaś ca (paraḥ paraṃ) smṛtaḥ
apūrvo 'nantaro 'bāhyo anaparaḥ praṇavo 'vyayaḥ //
meaning:
प्रणवो ह्य् अपरं ब्रह्म प्रणवश् च (परः परं) स्मृतः
अपूर्वो ऽनन्तरो ऽबाह्यो अनपरः प्रणवो ऽव्ययः //
text_mt:
The Praṇava is indeed the lower Brahman, and the Praṇava is remembered as the supreme;
without prior, without interior, without exterior, without posterior: the Praṇava is imperishable.

sanskrit_iast:
sarvasya praṇavo hy ādir madhyam antas tathaiva ca
evaṃ hi praṇavaṃ jñātvā vyaśnute tad anantaram //
meaning:
सर्वस्य प्रणवो ह्य् आदिर् मध्यम् अन्तस् तथैव च
एवं हि प्रणवं ज्ञात्वा व्यश्नुते तद् अनन्तरम् //
text_mt:
Praṇava is indeed the beginning, the middle, and likewise the end of all;
having known Praṇava thus, one attains that immediately.

sanskrit_iast:
praṇavaṃ hīśvaraṃ vidyāt sarvasya hṛdi saṃsthitam
sarvavyāpinam oṃkāraṃ matvā dhīro na śocati //
meaning:
प्रणवं हीश्वरं विद्यात् सर्वस्य हृदि संस्थितम्
सर्वव्यापिनम् ओंकारं मत्वा धीरो न शोचति //
text_mt:
One should know Praṇava as the Lord situated in the heart of all;
having known the all-pervading Omkāra, the wise one does not grieve.

sanskrit_iast:
amātro 'nantamātraś ca dvaitasyopaśamaḥ śivaḥ
oṃkāro vidito yena sa munir netaro janaḥ //
meaning:
अमात्रो ऽनन्तमात्रश् च द्वैतस्योपशमः शिवः
ओंकारो विदितो येन स मुनिर् नेतरो जनः //
text_mt:
The measureless, having endless morae, the cessation of duality, auspicious—
he by whom Omkāra is known is a sage, not any other person.

sanskrit_iast:
vaitathyaṃ sarvabhāvānāṃ svapne āhur manīṣiṇaḥ
antaḥsthānāt tu bhāvānāṃ saṃvṛtatvena hetunā //
meaning:
वैतथ्यं सर्वभावानां स्वप्ने आहुर् मनीषिणः
अन्तःस्थानात् तु भावानां संवृतत्वेन हेतुना //
text_mt:
The wise declare the unreality of all entities in a dream,
because the entities are situated inside, on account of their being enclosed.
title: (atha gauḍapādīya-kārikāyāṃ vaitathyā3khyaṃ dvitīyaṃ prakaraṇam [K:]dvitīyaṃ prakaraṇam [S:]vaitathya-prakaraṇam

sanskrit_iast:
adīrghatvāc ca kālasya gatvā deśān na paśyati
pratibuddhaś ca vai sarvas tasmin deśe na vidyate //
meaning:
अदीर्घत्वाच् च कालस्य गत्वा देशान् न पश्यति
प्रतिबुद्धश् च वै सर्वस् तस्मिन् देशे न विद्यते //
text_mt:
And because of the shortness of time, going [there], one does not see the places;
and everyone, upon waking up, is not in that place.

sanskrit_iast:
abhāvaś ca rathādīnāṃ śrūyate nyāyapūrvakam
vaitathyaṃ tena vai prāptaṃ svapne āhuḥ prakāśitam //
meaning:
अभावश् च रथादीनां श्रूयते न्यायपूर्वकम्
वैतथ्यं तेन वै प्राप्तं स्वप्ने आहुः प्रकाशितम् //
text_mt:
And the non-existence of chariots and the like is heard [in scripture], preceded by reasoning;
unreality is thereby indeed obtained [and] declared revealed in a dream.

sanskrit_iast:
antaḥsthānāt tu bhedānāṃ tasmāj jāgarite smṛtam
yathā tatra tathā svapne saṃvṛtatvena bhidyate //
meaning:
अन्तःस्थानात् तु भेदानां तस्माज् जागरिते स्मृतम्
यथा तत्र तथा स्वप्ने संवृतत्वेन भिद्यते //
text_mt:
Just as entities are situated inside [in a dream], so it is taught in the waking state;
as there, so in dream; enclosedness does not differ.

sanskrit_iast:
(svapnajāgaritasthāne [B,S:]svapnajāgarite sthāne) hy ekam āhur manīṣiṇaḥ
bhedānāṃ hi samatvena prasiddhenaiva hetunā //
meaning:
(स्वप्नजागरितस्थाने [ब्,स्:]स्वप्नजागरिते स्थाने) ह्य् एकम् आहुर् मनीषिणः
भेदानां हि समत्वेन प्रसिद्धेनैव हेतुना //
text_mt:
The wise declare the dream and waking states to be one,
on account of the established reason: the sameness of the differences.

sanskrit_iast:
ādāv ante ca yan nāsti vartamāne 'pi tat tathā
vitathaiḥ sadṛśāḥ santo avitathā iva lakṣitāḥ //
meaning:
आदाव् अन्ते च यन् नास्ति वर्तमाने ऽपि तत् तथा
वितथैः सदृशाः सन्तो अवितथा इव लक्षिताः //
text_mt:
That which does not exist in the beginning and in the end, exists likewise even in the present;
being like the unreal, they are perceived as if real.

sanskrit_iast:
saprayojanatā teṣāṃ svapne vipratipadyate
tasmād ādyantavattvena mithyaiva khalu te smṛtāḥ //
meaning:
सप्रयोजनता तेषां स्वप्ने विप्रतिपद्यते
तस्माद् आद्यन्तवत्त्वेन मिथ्यैव खलु ते स्मृताः //
text_mt:
Their serving a purpose is contradicted in a dream;
therefore, because of their having a beginning and an end, they are traditionally regarded as simply false.

sanskrit_iast:
apūrvaṃ sthānidharmo hi yathā svarganivāsinām
tān ayaṃ prekṣate gatvā yathaiveha suśikṣitaḥ //
meaning:
अपूर्वं स्थानिधर्मो हि यथा स्वर्गनिवासिनाम्
तान् अयं प्रेक्षते गत्वा यथैवेह सुशिक्षितः //
text_mt:
Indeed, extraordinary [objects] are the property of the state's dweller, as of the inhabitants of heaven;
going [there], he observes them just as one well-instructed here.

sanskrit_iast:
svapnavṛttāv api tv antaś cetasā kalpitaṃ tv asat
bahiś cetogṛhītaṃ sad dṛṣṭaṃ vaitathyam etayoḥ //
meaning:
स्वप्नवृत्ताव् अपि त्व् अन्तश् चेतसा कल्पितं त्व् असत्
बहिश् चेतोगृहीतं सद् दृष्टं वैतथ्यम् एतयोः //
text_mt:
In the occurrence of a dream, what is conceptually constructed inside by the mind is unreal,
while what is apprehended outside by the mind is real: the unreality of both is seen.

sanskrit_iast:
jāgradvṛttāv api tv antaś cetasā kalpitaṃ tv asat
bahiś cetogṛhītaṃ sad yuktaṃ vaitathyam etayoḥ //
meaning:
जाग्रद्वृत्ताव् अपि त्व् अन्तश् चेतसा कल्पितं त्व् असत्
बहिश् चेतोगृहीतं सद् युक्तं वैतथ्यम् एतयोः //
text_mt:
In the occurrence of the waking state, what is conceptually constructed inside by the mind is unreal,
while what is apprehended outside by the mind is real: the unreality of both is logical.

sanskrit_iast:
ubhayor api vaitathyaṃ bhedānāṃ sthānayor yadi
ka etān budhyate bhedān ko vai teṣāṃ vikalpakaḥ //
meaning:
उभयोर् अपि वैतथ्यं भेदानां स्थानयोर् यदि
क एतान् बुध्यते भेदान् को वै तेषां विकल्पकः //
text_mt:
If there is unreality of differences in both states,
who knows these differences? Who indeed is their conceptual constructor?

sanskrit_iast:
kalpayaty ātmanātmānam ātmā devaḥ svamāyayā
sa eva budhyate bhedān iti vedāntaniścayaḥ //
meaning:
कल्पयत्य् आत्मनात्मानम् आत्मा देवः स्वमायया
स एव बुध्यते भेदान् इति वेदान्तनिश्चयः //
text_mt:
The Self, the deity, conceptually constructs itself by itself through its own illusion;
it alone knows the differences: such is the settled conclusion of the Vedānta.

sanskrit_iast:
vikaroty aparān bhāvān antaś citte vyavasthitān
niyatāṃś ca bahiś citte evaṃ kalpayate prabhuḥ //
meaning:
विकरोत्य् अपरान् भावान् अन्तश् चित्ते व्यवस्थितान्
नियतांश् च बहिश् चित्ते एवं कल्पयते प्रभुः //
text_mt:
The Lord changes other entities settled within the mind,
and determinate ones in the mind outside: thus he conceptually constructs.

sanskrit_iast:
cittakālā hi ye 'ntas tu dvayakālāś ca ye bahiḥ
kalpitā eva te sarve viśeṣo nānyahetukaḥ //
meaning:
चित्तकाला हि ये ऽन्तस् तु द्वयकालाश् च ये बहिः
कल्पिता एव ते सर्वे विशेषो नान्यहेतुकः //
text_mt: Those [objects] that are within exist only for the duration of the mind, and those that are outside exist for the duration of two [points of observation]; / but all of them are merely conceptually constructed; their distinction has no other cause.

sanskrit_iast:
avyaktā eva ye 'ntas tu sphuṭā eva ca ye bahiḥ
kalpitā eva te sarve viśeṣas tv indriyāntare //
meaning:
अव्यक्ता एव ये ऽन्तस् तु स्फुटा एव च ये बहिः
कल्पिता एव ते सर्वे विशेषस् त्व् इन्द्रियान्तरे //
text_mt: Those [objects] that are within are unmanifest, and those that are outside are clear; / but all of them are merely conceptually constructed; their distinction lies only in the difference of sense organs.

sanskrit_iast:
jīvaṃ kalpayate pūrvaṃ tato bhāvān pṛthagvidhān
bāhyān ādhyātmikāṃś caiva yathāvidyas tathāsmṛtiḥ //
meaning:
जीवं कल्पयते पूर्वं ततो भावान् पृथग्विधान्
बाह्यान् आध्यात्मिकांश् चैव यथाविद्यस् तथास्मृतिः //
text_mt: First he conceptually constructs the individual soul, and then diverse entities, / both external and internal, [each] according to his knowledge and his memory.

sanskrit_iast:
aniścitā yathā rajjur andhakāre vikalpitā
sarpadhārādibhir bhāvais tadvad ātmā vikalpitaḥ //
meaning:
अनिश्चिता यथा रज्जुर् अन्धकारे विकल्पिता
सर्पधारादिभिर् भावैस् तद्वद् आत्मा विकल्पितः //
text_mt: Just as an unascertained rope is conceptually constructed in the dark / as various entities such as a snake or a stream of water, so is the Self conceptually constructed.

sanskrit_iast:
niścitāyāṃ yathā rajjvāṃ vikalpo vinivartate
rajjur eveti cādvaitaṃ tadvad ātmaviniścayaḥ //
meaning:
निश्चितायां यथा रज्ज्वां विकल्पो विनिवर्तते
रज्जुर् एवेति चाद्वैतं तद्वद् आत्मविनिश्चयः //
text_mt: Just as, when the rope is ascertained, conceptual construction ceases / and the non-dual [thought arises] that "it is just a rope," so is the ascertainment of the Self.

sanskrit_iast:
prāṇādibhir (anantaiś ca [B,S:]anantais tu) bhāvair etair vikalpitaḥ
māyaiṣā tasya devasya (yayā saṃmohitaḥ [B,S:]yayāyaṃ mohitaḥ) svayam //
meaning:
प्राणादिभिर् (अनन्तैश् च [ब्,स्:]अनन्तैस् तु) भावैर् एतैर् विकल्पितः
मायैषा तस्य देवस्य (यया संमोहितः [ब्,स्:]ययायं मोहितः) स्वयम् //
text_mt: He is conceptually constructed as these endless entities such as the vital breaths; / this is the illusion of that divine being, by which he himself is deluded.

sanskrit_iast:
prāṇa iti prāṇavido bhūtānīti ca tadvidaḥ
guṇā iti guṇavidas tattvānīti ca tadvidaḥ //
meaning:
प्राण इति प्राणविदो भूतानीति च तद्विदः
गुणा इति गुणविदस् तत्त्वानीति च तद्विदः //
text_mt: [He is] the vital breath, say the knowers of the vital breath; the elements, say the knowers of the elements; / the qualities, say the knowers of the qualities; the principles, say the knowers of the principles;

sanskrit_iast:
pādā iti pādavido viṣayā iti tadvidaḥ
lokā iti lokavido devā iti ca tadvidaḥ //
meaning:
पादा इति पादविदो विषया इति तद्विदः
लोका इति लोकविदो देवा इति च तद्विदः //
text_mt: the quarters, say the knowers of the quarters; the sense objects, say the knowers of the sense objects; / the worlds, say the knowers of the worlds; and the gods, say the knowers of the gods;

sanskrit_iast:
vedā iti vedavido yajñā iti ca tadvidaḥ
bhokteti ca bhoktṛvido bhojyam iti ca tadvidaḥ //
meaning:
वेदा इति वेदविदो यज्ञा इति च तद्विदः
भोक्तेति च भोक्तृविदो भोज्यम् इति च तद्विदः //
text_mt: the Vedas, say the knowers of the Vedas; the sacrifices, say the knowers of the sacrifices; / the experiencer, say the knowers of the experiencer; and the experienced, say the knowers of the experienced;

sanskrit_iast:
sūkṣma iti sūkṣmavidaḥ sthūla iti ca tadvidaḥ
mūrta iti mūrtavido amūrta iti ca tadvidaḥ //
meaning:
सूक्ष्म इति सूक्ष्मविदः स्थूल इति च तद्विदः
मूर्त इति मूर्तविदो अमूर्त इति च तद्विदः //
text_mt: subtle, say the knowers of the subtle; gross, say the knowers of the gross; / formed, say the knowers of the formed; and formless, say the knowers of the formless;

sanskrit_iast:
kāla iti kālavido diśa iti ca tadvidaḥ
vādā iti vādavido bhuvanānīti tadvidaḥ //
meaning:
काल इति कालविदो दिश इति च तद्विदः
वादा इति वादविदो भुवनानीति तद्विदः //
text_mt: time, say the knowers of time; the directions, say the knowers of the directions; / doctrines, say the knowers of doctrines; the realms, say the knowers of the realms;

sanskrit_iast:
mana iti manovido buddhir iti ca tadvidaḥ
cittam iti cittavido dharmādharmau ca tadvidaḥ //
meaning:
मन इति मनोविदो बुद्धिर् इति च तद्विदः
चित्तम् इति चित्तविदो धर्माधर्मौ च तद्विदः //
text_mt: mind, say the knowers of mind; intellect, say the knowers of intellect; / consciousness, say the knowers of consciousness; and virtue and vice, say their knowers;

sanskrit_iast:
pañcaviṃśaka ity eke ṣaḍviṃśa iti cāpare
ekatriṃśaka ity āhur ananta iti cāpare //
meaning:
पञ्चविंशक इत्य् एके षड्विंश इति चापरे
एकत्रिंशक इत्य् आहुर् अनन्त इति चापरे //
text_mt: some say twenty-five [principles], others twenty-six, / others say thirty-one, and still others say infinite;

sanskrit_iast:
lokāṃl lokavidaḥ prāhur āśramā iti tadvidaḥ
strīpuṃnapuṃsakaṃ laiṅgāḥ parāparam athāpare //
meaning:
लोकांल् लोकविदः प्राहुर् आश्रमा इति तद्विदः
स्त्रीपुंनपुंसकं लैङ्गाः परापरम् अथापरे //
text_mt: the worlds, say the knowers of the worlds; the stages of life, say their knowers; / female, male, and neuter, say the grammarians; others say higher and lower;

sanskrit_iast:
sṛṣṭir iti sṛṣṭivido laya iti ca tadvidaḥ
sthitir iti sthitividaḥ sarve ceha tu sarvadā //
meaning:
सृष्टिर् इति सृष्टिविदो लय इति च तद्विदः
स्थितिर् इति स्थितिविदः सर्वे चेह तु सर्वदा //
text_mt: creation, say the knowers of creation; dissolution, say the knowers of dissolution; / maintenance, say the knowers of maintenance; but all these are [conceived] here at all times.

sanskrit_iast:
yaṃ bhāvaṃ darśayed yasya taṃ bhāvaṃ sa tu paśyati
taṃ cāvati sa bhūtvāsau tadgrahaḥ samupaiti tam //
meaning:
यं भावं दर्शयेद् यस्य तं भावं स तु पश्यति
तं चावति स भूत्वासौ तद्ग्रहः समुपैति तम् //
text_mt: Whatever entity one presents to someone, that entity he sees; / and having become that, he protects it; clinging to it overtakes him.

sanskrit_iast:
etair eṣo apṛthagbhāvaiḥ pṛthag eveti lakṣitaḥ
evaṃ yo veda tattvena kalpayet so 'viśaṅkitaḥ //
meaning:
एतैर् एषो अपृथग्भावैः पृथग् एवेति लक्षितः
एवं यो वेद तत्त्वेन कल्पयेत् सो ऽविशङ्कितः //
text_mt: Through these entities that are not distinct [from him], he is perceived as distinct; / he who knows this in truth may conceptually construct without hesitation.

sanskrit_iast:
svapnamāye yathā dṛṣṭe gandharvanagaraṃ yathā
tathā viśvam idaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ vedānteṣu vicakṣaṇaiḥ //
meaning:
स्वप्नमाये यथा दृष्टे गन्धर्वनगरं यथा
तथा विश्वम् इदं दृष्टं वेदान्तेषु विचक्षणैः //
text_mt: As a dream and an illusion are seen, as a city of the Gandharvas is seen, / so is this whole universe seen by those discerning in the Upaniṣads.

sanskrit_iast:
na nirodho na cotpattir na baddho na ca sādhakaḥ
na mumukṣur na vai mukta ity eṣā paramārthatā //
meaning:
न निरोधो न चोत्पत्तिर् न बद्धो न च साधकः
न मुमुक्षुर् न वै मुक्त इत्य् एषा परमार्थता //
text_mt: There is no cessation and no arising, no one bound and no practitioner, / no seeker of liberation and none indeed liberated: this is the ultimate truth.

sanskrit_iast:
bhāvair asadbhir evāyam advayena ca kalpitaḥ
bhāvā apy advayenaiva tasmād advayatā śivā //
meaning:
भावैर् असद्भिर् एवायम् अद्वयेन च कल्पितः
भावा अप्य् अद्वयेनैव तस्माद् अद्वयता शिवा //
text_mt: This [Self] is conceptually constructed by unreal entities and as non-dual; / the entities also [are perceived] solely by virtue of the non-dual; therefore non-duality is auspicious.

sanskrit_iast:
nātmabhāvena nānedaṃ na svenāpi kathaṃcana
na pṛthaṅ nāpṛthak kiṃcid iti tattvavido viduḥ //
meaning:
नात्मभावेन नानेदं न स्वेनापि कथंचन
न पृथङ् नापृथक् किंचिद् इति तत्त्वविदो विदुः //
text_mt: This manifold is not real as the Self, nor in any way by its own nature; / nothing is separate, nor is anything non-separate: so the knowers of truth understand.

sanskrit_iast:
vītarāgabhayakrodhair munibhir vedapāragaiḥ
nirvikalpo hy ayaṃ dṛṣṭaḥ prapañcopaśamo 'dvayaḥ //
meaning:
वीतरागभयक्रोधैर् मुनिभिर् वेदपारगैः
निर्विकल्पो ह्य् अयं दृष्टः प्रपञ्चोपशमो ऽद्वयः //
text_mt: By sages free from passion, fear, and anger, who have traversed the Vedas, / this has been seen as free from conceptual construction, the cessation of phenomenal manifestation, non-dual.

sanskrit_iast:
tasmād evaṃ viditvainam advaite yojayet smṛtim
advaitaṃ samanuprāpya jaḍaval lokam ācaret //
meaning:
तस्माद् एवं विदित्वैनम् अद्वैते योजयेत् स्मृतिम्
अद्वैतं समनुप्राप्य जडवल् लोकम् आचरेत् //
text_mt: Therefore, knowing it thus, one should fix one's remembrance on non-duality; / having fully attained non-duality, one should move among people as if inert.

sanskrit_iast:
niḥstutir nirnamaskāro niḥsvadhākāra eva ca
calācalaniketaś ca yatir yādṛcchiko bhavet //
meaning:
निःस्तुतिर् निर्नमस्कारो निःस्वधाकार एव च
चलाचलनिकेतश् च यतिर् यादृच्छिको भवेत् //
text_mt: Without praise, without salutation, and without offering to the ancestors, / having the moving and the unmoving as his dwelling, the ascetic should live as chance dictates.

sanskrit_iast:
tattvam ādhyātmikaṃ dṛṣṭvā tattvaṃ dṛṣṭvā tu bāhyataḥ
tattvībhūtas tadārāmas tattvād apracyuto bhavet //
atha gauḍapādīya-kārikāsv a-dvaitā3khyaṃ tṛtīyaṃ prakaraṇam | oṃ
meaning:
तत्त्वम् आध्यात्मिकं दृष्ट्वा तत्त्वं दृष्ट्वा तु बाह्यतः
तत्त्वीभूतस् तदारामस् तत्त्वाद् अप्रच्युतो भवेत् //
अथ गौडपादीय-कारिकास्व् अ-द्वैता3ख्यं तृतीयं प्रकरणम् | ओं
text_mt:
Having seen the truth internally and having seen the truth externally, / having become the truth and delighting in it, one should not deviate from the truth.
Now begins the third chapter, named "Non-duality," in the verses of Gauḍapāda. Om.

sanskrit_iast:
upāsanāśrito dharmo jāte brahmaṇi vartate
prāg utpatter ajaṃ sarvaṃ tenāsau kṛpaṇaḥ smṛtaḥ //
meaning:
उपासनाश्रितो धर्मो जाते ब्रह्मणि वर्तते
प्राग् उत्पत्तेर् अजं सर्वं तेनासौ कृपणः स्मृतः //
text_mt: The individual soul relying on worship attaches itself to an originated Brahman; / prior to origination, everything is unborn; therefore such a person is deemed pitiful.

sanskrit_iast:
ato vakṣyāmy akārpaṇyam ajāti samatāṃ gatam
yathā na jāyate kiṃcij jāyamānaṃ samantataḥ //
meaning:
अतो वक्ष्याम्य् अकार्पण्यम् अजाति समतां गतम्
यथा न जायते किंचिज् जायमानं समन्ततः //
text_mt: Therefore I shall declare the unpitiful state, non-origination, attained to sameness, / in which nothing whatsoever is born, though appearing to be born on every side.

sanskrit_iast:
ātmā hy ākāśavaj jīvair ghaṭākāśair ivoditaḥ
ghaṭādivac ca saṃghātair jātāv etan nidarśanam //
meaning:
आत्मा ह्य् आकाशवज् जीवैर् घटाकाशैर् इवोदितः
घटादिवच् च संघातैर् जाताव् एतन् निदर्शनम् //
text_mt: For the Self is declared [to exist] through the individual souls as space [exists] through pot-spaces, / and through the aggregates as through pots and the like; this is the illustration regarding origination.

sanskrit_iast:
ghaṭādiṣu pralīneṣu ghaṭākāśādayo yathā
ākāśe saṃpralīyante tadvaj jīvā ihātmani //
meaning:
घटादिषु प्रलीनेषु घटाकाशादयो यथा
आकाशे संप्रलीयन्ते तद्वज् जीवा इहात्मनि //
text_mt: Just as, when pots and the like dissolve, the pot-spaces and the like / dissolve into space, so in this world do the individual souls [dissolve] into the Self.

sanskrit_iast:
yathaikasmin ghaṭākāśe rajodhūmādibhir yute
na sarve saṃprayujyante tadvaj jīvāḥ sukhādibhiḥ //
meaning:
यथैकस्मिन् घटाकाशे रजोधूमादिभिर् युते
न सर्वे संप्रयुज्यन्ते तद्वज् जीवाः सुखादिभिः //
text_mt: Just as, when one pot-space is filled with dust, smoke, and the like, / not all are joined with them, so it is with individual souls regarding pleasure and the like.

sanskrit_iast:
rūpakāryasamākhyāś ca bhidyante tatra tatra vai
ākāśasya na bhedo 'sti tadvaj jīveṣu nirṇayaḥ //
meaning:
रूपकार्यसमाख्याश् च भिद्यन्ते तत्र तत्र वै
आकाशस्य न भेदो ऽस्ति तद्वज् जीवेषु निर्णयः //
text_mt: Forms, functions, and names indeed differ here and there, / but there is no difference in space; such is the conclusion regarding individual souls.

sanskrit_iast:
nākāśasya ghaṭākāśo vikārāvayavau yathā
naivātmanaḥ sadā jīvo vikārāvayavau tathā //
meaning:
नाकाशस्य घटाकाशो विकारावयवौ यथा
नैवात्मनः सदा जीवो विकारावयवौ तथा //
text_mt: Just as pot-space is neither a modification nor a part of space, / so the individual soul is never a modification or a part of the Self.

sanskrit_iast:
yathā bhavati bālānāṃ gaganaṃ malinaṃ malaiḥ
tathā bhavaty abuddhānām ātmāpi malino malaiḥ //
meaning:
यथा भवति बालानां गगनं मलिनं मलैः
तथा भवत्य् अबुद्धानाम् आत्मापि मलिनो मलैः //
text_mt: Just as the sky appears soiled with impurities to children, / so the Self also appears soiled with impurities to the unawakened.

sanskrit_iast:
maraṇe saṃbhave caiva gatyāgamanayor api
sthitau sarvaśarīreṣu (ākāśenā[K,S:]cākāśenā)vilakṣaṇaḥ [CHECK!] //
meaning:
मरणे संभवे चैव गत्यागमनयोर् अपि
स्थितौ सर्वशरीरेषु (आकाशेना[क्,स्:]चाकाशेना)विलक्षणः [छेच्क्!] //
text_mt: In dying and in being born, in going and coming as well, / and in existing in all bodies, [the Self] is not different from space.

sanskrit_iast:
saṃghātāḥ svapnavat (sarve sarve) ātmamāyāvisarjitāḥ [CHECK!]
ādhikye sarvasāmye vā nopapattir hi vidyate //
meaning:
संघाताः स्वप्नवत् (सर्वे सर्वे) आत्ममायाविसर्जिताः [छेच्क्!]
आधिक्ये सर्वसाम्ये वा नोपपत्तिर् हि विद्यते //
text_mt: All aggregates are like a dream, projected by the illusion of the Self; / for there is no rational demonstration whether they are superior or completely equal.

sanskrit_iast:
rasādayo hi ye kośā vyākhyātās taittirīyake
teṣāṃ ātmā paro jīvaḥ khaṃ yathā saṃprakāśitaḥ //
meaning:
रसादयो हि ये कोशा व्याख्यातास् तैत्तिरीयके
तेषां आत्मा परो जीवः खं यथा संप्रकाशितः //
text_mt: The sheaths, consisting of food and the rest, which are expounded in the Taittirīya, / their supreme Self is the individual soul, illuminated just like space.

sanskrit_iast:
dvayor dvayor madhujñāne paraṃ brahma prakāśitam
pṛthivyām udare caiva yathākāśaḥ prakāśitaḥ //
meaning:
द्वयोर् द्वयोर् मधुज्ञाने परं ब्रह्म प्रकाशितम्
पृथिव्याम् उदरे चैव यथाकाशः प्रकाशितः //
text_mt: In each pair [in the section on] the knowledge of honey, the supreme Brahman is illuminated, / just as space is illuminated in the earth and in the belly.

sanskrit_iast:
jīvātmanor ananyatvam abhedena praśasyate
nānātvaṃ nindyate yac ca tad evaṃ hi samañjasam //
meaning:
जीवात्मनोर् अनन्यत्वम् अभेदेन प्रशस्यते
नानात्वं निन्द्यते यच् च तद् एवं हि समञ्जसम् //
text_mt: The non-otherness of the individual soul and the Self is praised through non-difference, / and multiplicity is condemned; for that alone is consistent with reason.

sanskrit_iast:
jīvātmanoḥ pṛthaktvaṃ yat prāg utpatteḥ prakīrtitam
bhaviṣyadvṛttyā gauṇaṃ tan mukhyatvaṃ hi na yujyate //
meaning:
जीवात्मनोः पृथक्त्वं यत् प्राग् उत्पत्तेः प्रकीर्तितम्
भविष्यद्वृत्त्या गौणं तन् मुख्यत्वं हि न युज्यते //
text_mt: The separateness of the individual soul and the Self that is stated prior to origination / is figurative, referring to future states; primary meaning is not tenable.

sanskrit_iast:
mṛllohavisphuliṅgādyaiḥ sṛṣṭir yā coditānyathā
upāyaḥ so 'vatārāya nāsti bhedaḥ kathaṃcana //
meaning:
मृल्लोहविस्फुलिङ्गाद्यैः सृष्टिर् या चोदितान्यथा
उपायः सो ऽवताराय नास्ति भेदः कथंचन //
text_mt: The creation that has been taught in various ways by means of clay, iron, sparks, and so forth / is an expedient for introducing [the truth]; there is no difference whatsoever.

sanskrit_iast:
āśramās trividhā hīnamadhyamotkṛṣṭadṛṣṭayaḥ
upāsanopadiṣṭeyaṃ tadartham anukampayā //
meaning:
आश्रमास् त्रिविधा हीनमध्यमोत्कृष्टदृष्टयः
उपासनोपदिष्टेयं तदर्थम् अनुकम्पया //
text_mt: The stages of life are of three kinds, with low, middling, and superior perspectives; / this worship was taught for their sake out of compassion.

sanskrit_iast:
svasiddhāntavyavasthāsu dvaitino niścitā dṛḍham
parasparaṃ virudhyante tair ayaṃ na virudhyate //
meaning:
स्वसिद्धान्तव्यवस्थासु द्वैतिनो निश्चिता दृढम्
परस्परं विरुध्यन्ते तैर् अयं न विरुध्यते //
text_mt: Firmly settled in the conclusions of their own doctrines, the dualists / conflict with one another; this [doctrine] does not conflict with them.

sanskrit_iast:
advaitaṃ paramārtho hi dvaitaṃ tadbheda ucyate
teṣām ubhayathā dvaitaṃ tenāyaṃ na virudhyate //
meaning:
अद्वैतं परमार्थो हि द्वैतं तद्भेद उच्यते
तेषाम् उभयथा द्वैतं तेनायं न विरुध्यते //
text_mt: For non-duality is the ultimate truth, and duality is said to be its distinction; / for them, duality exists in both ways; therefore this [doctrine] does not conflict [with them].

sanskrit_iast:
māyayā bhidyate hy etan nānyathājaṃ kathaṃcana
tattvato bhidyamāne hi martyatām amṛtaṃ vrajet //
meaning:
मायया भिद्यते ह्य् एतन् नान्यथाजं कथंचन
तत्त्वतो भिद्यमाने हि मर्त्यताम् अमृतं व्रजेत् //
text_mt: For this [unborn] is differentiated only through illusion, not otherwise in any way; / for if it were differentiated in reality, the immortal would pass into mortality.

sanskrit_iast:
ajātasyaiva bhāvasya jātim icchanti vādinaḥ
ajāto hy amṛto bhāvo martyatāṃ katham eṣyati //
meaning:
अजातस्यैव भावस्य जातिम् इच्छन्ति वादिनः
अजातो ह्य् अमृतो भावो मर्त्यतां कथम् एष्यति //
text_mt: Disputants assert the origination of that very entity which is unborn; / but how will an unborn, immortal entity pass into mortality?

sanskrit_iast:
na bhavaty amṛtaṃ martyaṃ na martyam amṛtaṃ tathā
prakṛter anyathābhāvo na kathaṃcid bhaviṣyati //
meaning:
न भवत्य् अमृतं मर्त्यं न मर्त्यम् अमृतं तथा
प्रकृतेर् अन्यथाभावो न कथंचिद् भविष्यति //
text_mt: The immortal does not become mortal, nor does the mortal become immortal; / there will never in any way be an alteration of inherent nature.

sanskrit_iast:
svabhāvenāmṛto yasya bhāvo gacchati martyatām
kṛtakenāmṛtas tasya kathaṃ sthāsyati niścalaḥ //
meaning:
स्वभावेनामृतो यस्य भावो गच्छति मर्त्यताम्
कृतकेनामृतस् तस्य कथं स्थास्यति निश्चलः //
text_mt: If one's entity is immortal by own-nature and undergoes mortality, / how will it, made immortal through an artificial condition, remain motionless?

sanskrit_iast:
bhūtato 'bhūtato vāpi sṛjyamāne samā śrutiḥ
niścitaṃ yuktiyuktaṃ ca yat tad bhavati netarat //
meaning:
भूततो ऽभूततो वापि सृज्यमाने समा श्रुतिः
निश्चितं युक्तियुक्तं च यत् तद् भवति नेतरत् //
text_mt: Whether creation proceeds from that which exists or does not exist, scripture speaks equally. / That which is ascertained and endowed with reason is the reality, not anything else.

sanskrit_iast:
neha nāneti cāmnāyād indro māyābhir ity api
ajāyamāno bahudhā māyayā jāyate tu saḥ //
meaning:
नेह नानेति चाम्नायाद् इन्द्रो मायाभिर् इत्य् अपि
अजायमानो बहुधा मायया जायते तु सः //
text_mt: And from the scriptural teaching, 'There is no diversity here,' and also, 'Indra through illusions…' / though unborn, he is indeed born manifoldly through illusion.

sanskrit_iast:
saṃbhūter apavādāc ca saṃbhavaḥ pratiṣidhyate
ko (nv [K,B,S:]tv) enaṃ janayed iti kāraṇaṃ pratiṣidhyate [CHECK!] //
meaning:
संभूतेर् अपवादाच् च संभवः प्रतिषिध्यते
को (न्व् [क्,ब्,स्:]त्व्) एनं जनयेद् इति कारणं प्रतिषिध्यते [छेच्क्!] //
text_mt: And by the censure of manifestation, origination is negated; / 'Who then could generate this?'—by this, the cause is negated.

sanskrit_iast:
sa eṣa neti netīti vyākhyātaṃ nihnute yataḥ
sarvam agrāhyabhāvena hetunājaṃ prakāśate //
meaning:
स एष नेति नेतीति व्याख्यातं निह्नुते यतः
सर्वम् अग्राह्यभावेन हेतुनाजं प्रकाशते //
text_mt: Since that [scripture], stating 'not this, not this,' denies whatever has been explained, / the unborn [Self] shines forth of itself by reason of being ungraspable.

sanskrit_iast:
sato hi māyayā janma yujyate na tu tattvataḥ
tattvato jāyate yasya jātaṃ tasya hi jāyate //
meaning:
सतो हि मायया जन्म युज्यते न तु तत्त्वतः
तत्त्वतो जायते यस्य जातं तस्य हि जायते //
text_mt: Birth through illusion is indeed plausible for what exists, but not in reality; / for one to whom it is born in reality, that which is already born would be born.

sanskrit_iast:
asato māyayā janma tattvato naiva yujyate
vandhyāputro na tattvena māyayā vāpi jāyate //
meaning:
असतो मायया जन्म तत्त्वतो नैव युज्यते
वन्ध्यापुत्रो न तत्त्वेन मायया वापि जायते //
text_mt: Birth through illusion is not plausible at all for what does not exist, neither in reality; / the son of a barren woman is born neither in reality nor through illusion.

sanskrit_iast:
yathā svapne dvayābhāsaṃ spandate māyayā manaḥ
tathā jāgraddvayābhāsaṃ spandate māyayā manaḥ //
meaning:
यथा स्वप्ने द्वयाभासं स्पन्दते मायया मनः
तथा जाग्रद्द्वयाभासं स्पन्दते मायया मनः //
text_mt: Just as the mind moves in the dream state as an appearance of duality through illusion, / so the mind moves in the waking state as an appearance of duality through illusion.

sanskrit_iast:
advayaṃ ca dvayābhāsaṃ manaḥ svapne na saṃśayaḥ
advayaṃ ca dvayābhāsaṃ tathā jāgran na saṃśayaḥ //
meaning:
अद्वयं च द्वयाभासं मनः स्वप्ने न संशयः
अद्वयं च द्वयाभासं तथा जाग्रन् न संशयः //
text_mt: And the non-dual mind is an appearance of duality in the dream state, without doubt; / and the non-dual mind is likewise an appearance of duality in the waking state, without doubt.

sanskrit_iast:
manodṛśyam idaṃ dvaitaṃ yat kiṃcit sacarācaram
manaso hy amanībhāve dvaitaṃ naivopalabhyate //
meaning:
मनोदृश्यम् इदं द्वैतं यत् किंचित् सचराचरम्
मनसो ह्य् अमनीभावे द्वैतं नैवोपलभ्यते //
text_mt: All this duality, whatever is moving or unmoving, is perceptible only to the mind; / for when the mind ceases to be mind, duality is not apprehended at all.

sanskrit_iast:
ātmasatyānubodhena na saṃkalpayate yadā
amanastāṃ tadā yāti grāhyābhāve tad agraham //
meaning:
आत्मसत्यानुबोधेन न संकल्पयते यदा
अमनस्तां तदा याति ग्राह्याभावे तद् अग्रहम् //
text_mt: When it does not conceptually construct due to realization of the truth of the Self, / it then goes to the state of non-mind; in the absence of an object to be grasped, it is without grasping.

sanskrit_iast:
akalpakam ajaṃ jñānaṃ jñeyābhinnaṃ pracakṣate
brahma jñeyam ajaṃ nityam ajenājaṃ vibudhyate //
meaning:
अकल्पकम् अजं ज्ञानं ज्ञेयाभिन्नं प्रचक्षते
ब्रह्म ज्ञेयम् अजं नित्यम् अजेनाजं विबुध्यते //
text_mt: They declare that knowledge is free of conceptual construction, unborn, and non-different from the knowable; / Brahman is the knowable, unborn and eternal; by the unborn, the unborn is known.

sanskrit_iast:
nigṛhītasya manaso nirvikalpasya dhīmataḥ
pracāraḥ sa tu vijñeyaḥ suṣupte 'nyo na tatsamaḥ //
meaning:
निगृहीतस्य मनसो निर्विकल्पस्य धीमतः
प्रचारः स तु विज्ञेयः सुषुप्ते ऽन्यो न तत्समः //
text_mt: The functioning of the restrained mind of the wise one, free from conceptual construction, / is to be known as such; in deep sleep it is different, not equal to that.

sanskrit_iast:
līyate hi suṣupte tan nigṛhītaṃ na līyate
tad eva nirbhayaṃ brahma jñānālokaṃ samantataḥ //
meaning:
लीयते हि सुषुप्ते तन् निगृहीतं न लीयते
तद् एव निर्भयं ब्रह्म ज्ञानालोकं समन्ततः //
text_mt: For in deep sleep it dissolves, but when restrained it does not dissolve; / that very state is fearless Brahman, with the light of knowledge all around.

sanskrit_iast:
ajam anidram asvapnam anāmakam arūpakam
sakṛdvibhātaṃ sarvajñaṃ nopacāraḥ kathaṃcana //
meaning:
अजम् अनिद्रम् अस्वप्नम् अनामकम् अरूपकम्
सकृद्विभातं सर्वज्ञं नोपचारः कथंचन //
text_mt: Unborn, sleepless, dreamless, nameless, formless, / ever-luminous, omniscient—there is no figurative usage whatsoever.

sanskrit_iast:
sarvābhilāpavigataḥ sarvacintāsamutthitaḥ
supraśāntaḥ sakṛjjyotiḥ samādhir acalo 'bhayaḥ //
meaning:
सर्वाभिलापविगतः सर्वचिन्तासमुत्थितः
सुप्रशान्तः सकृज्ज्योतिः समाधिर् अचलो ऽभयः //
text_mt: Departed from all verbal expression, risen above all thought, / exceedingly tranquil, constant light, samādhi, unmoving, fearless.

sanskrit_iast:
graho na tatra notsargaś cintā yatra na vidyate
ātmasaṃsthaṃ tadā jñānam ajāti samatāṃ gatam //
meaning:
ग्रहो न तत्र नोत्सर्गश् चिन्ता यत्र न विद्यते
आत्मसंस्थं तदा ज्ञानम् अजाति समतां गतम् //
text_mt: There is no grasping and no giving up where thought does not exist; / then knowledge rests in the Self, non-origination having attained sameness.

sanskrit_iast:
asparśayogo vai nāma durdarśaḥ sarvayogibhiḥ
yogino bibhyati hy asmād abhaye bhayadarśinaḥ //
meaning:
अस्पर्शयोगो वै नाम दुर्दर्शः सर्वयोगिभिः
योगिनो बिभ्यति ह्य् अस्माद् अभये भयदर्शिनः //
text_mt: This indeed is called the yoga of non-contact, difficult to be seen by all yogins; / for yogins are afraid of it, seeing fear in the fearless.

sanskrit_iast:
manaso nigrahāyattam abhayaṃ sarvayogiṇām
duḥkhakṣayaḥ prabodhaś cāpy akṣayā śāntir eva ca //
meaning:
मनसो निग्रहायत्तम् अभयं सर्वयोगिणाम्
दुःखक्षयः प्रबोधश् चाप्य् अक्षया शान्तिर् एव च //
text_mt: The fearlessness of all yogins depends on restraint of the mind, / as do the destruction of suffering, awakening, and imperishable peace.

sanskrit_iast:
utseka udadher yadvat kuśāgreṇaikabindunā
manaso nigrahas tadvad bhaved aparikhedataḥ //
meaning:
उत्सेक उदधेर् यद्वत् कुशाग्रेणैकबिन्दुना
मनसो निग्रहस् तद्वद् भवेद् अपरिखेदतः //
text_mt: Just as the emptying of the ocean could be done drop by drop with the tip of a kuśa grass, / so the restraint of the mind should proceed without weariness.

sanskrit_iast:
upāyena nigṛhṇīyād vikṣiptaṃ kāmabhogayoḥ
suprasannaṃ laye caiva yathā kāmo layas tathā //
meaning:
उपायेन निगृह्णीयाद् विक्षिप्तं कामभोगयोः
सुप्रसन्नं लये चैव यथा कामो लयस् तथा //
text_mt: By skillful means one should restrain it when distracted in desires and pleasures, / and also when fully calmed in dissolution; for as desire is, so is dissolution.

sanskrit_iast:
duḥkhaṃ sarvam anusmṛtya kāmabhogān nivartayet
ajaṃ sarvam anusmṛtya jātaṃ naiva tu paśyati //
meaning:
दुःखं सर्वम् अनुस्मृत्य कामभोगान् निवर्तयेत्
अजं सर्वम् अनुस्मृत्य जातं नैव तु पश्यति //
text_mt: Remembering that everything is suffering, one should turn back from desire's enjoyments; / remembering that everything is unborn, one does not see what is born at all.

sanskrit_iast:
laye saṃbodhayec cittaṃ vikṣiptaṃ śamayet punaḥ
sakaṣāyaṃ vijānīyāt samaprāptaṃ na cālayet //
meaning:
लये संबोधयेच् चित्तं विक्षिप्तं शमयेत् पुनः
सकषायं विजानीयात् समप्राप्तं न चालयेत् //
text_mt: One should awaken the mind in dissolution, and quiet it again when distracted; / one should recognize it when it has attachment, and not agitate it when it has reached equipoise.

sanskrit_iast:
nāsvādayet sukhaṃ tatra niḥsaṅgaḥ prajñayā bhavet
niścalaṃ niścarat cittam ekīkuryāt prayatnataḥ //
meaning:
नास्वादयेत् सुखं तत्र निःसङ्गः प्रज्ञया भवेत्
निश्चलं निश्चरत् चित्तम् एकीकुर्यात् प्रयत्नतः //
text_mt: One should not taste pleasure there; one should become unattached through discernment; / with effort one should unify the mind, making it motionless when it wanders.

sanskrit_iast:
yadā na līyate cittaṃ na ca vikṣipyate punaḥ
aniṅganam anābhāsaṃ niṣpannaṃ brahma tat tadā //
meaning:
यदा न लीयते चित्तं न च विक्षिप्यते पुनः
अनिङ्गनम् अनाभासं निष्पन्नं ब्रह्म तत् तदा //
text_mt: When the mind does not dissolve and is not distracted again, / motionless, free of appearance, then it has become Brahman.

sanskrit_iast:
svasthaṃ śāntaṃ sanirvāṇam akathyaṃ sukham uttamam
ajam ajena jñeyena sarvajñaṃ paricakṣate //
meaning:
स्वस्थं शान्तं सनिर्वाणम् अकथ्यं सुखम् उत्तमम्
अजम् अजेन ज्ञेयेन सर्वज्ञं परिचक्षते //
text_mt: Resting in itself, tranquil, with extinction, ineffable, supreme bliss, / unborn, omniscient through the unborn knowable—so they declare.

sanskrit_iast:
na kaścij jāyate jīvaḥ saṃbhavo 'sya na vidyate
etat tad uttamaṃ satyaṃ yatra kiṃcin na jāyate //
meaning:
न कश्चिज् जायते जीवः संभवो ऽस्य न विद्यते
एतत् तद् उत्तमं सत्यं यत्र किंचिन् न जायते //
text_mt: No individual soul whatsoever is born; no manifestation belongs to it; / this is that supreme truth, where nothing whatsoever is born.

sanskrit_iast:
jñānenākāśakalpena dharmān yo gaganopamān
jñeyābhinnena saṃbuddhas taṃ vande dvipadāṃ varam //
meaning:
ज्ञानेनाकाशकल्पेन धर्मान् यो गगनोपमान्
ज्ञेयाभिन्नेन संबुद्धस् तं वन्दे द्विपदां वरम् //
text_mt: I revere him, the best of two-legged beings, who through knowledge like empty space / became fully awakened to the entities resembling the sky, non-different from the knowable.
title: athā7lāta-śānty-ākhyaṃ caturtha-prakaraṇam

sanskrit_iast:
asparśayogo vai nāma sarvasattvasukho hitaḥ
avivādo aviruddhaś ca deśitas taṃ namāmy aham //
meaning:
अस्पर्शयोगो वै नाम सर्वसत्त्वसुखो हितः
अविवादो अविरुद्धश् च देशितस् तं नमाम्य् अहम् //
text_mt: I bow down to that yoga of non-contact which has been taught, / delightful for all beings, beneficial, free of disputation, and uncontradicted.

sanskrit_iast:
bhūtasya jātim icchanti vādinaḥ kecid eva hi
abhūtasyāpare dhīrā vivadantaḥ parasparam //
meaning:
भूतस्य जातिम् इच्छन्ति वादिनः केचिद् एव हि
अभूतस्यापरे धीरा विवदन्तः परस्परम् //
text_mt: Some disputants indeed maintain the birth of what exists, / while other wise ones maintain that of what does not exist, disputing with one another.

sanskrit_iast:
bhūtaṃ na jāyate kiṃcid abhūtaṃ naiva jāyate
vivadanto dvayā hy evam ajātiṃ khyāpayanti te //
meaning:
भूतं न जायते किंचिद् अभूतं नैव जायते
विवदन्तो द्वया ह्य् एवम् अजातिं ख्यापयन्ति ते //
text_mt: What exists is not born at all, nor is what does not exist born at all; / thus disputing, they proclaim non-origination.

sanskrit_iast:
khyāpyamānām ajātiṃ tair anumodāmahe vayam
vivadāmo na taiḥ sārdham avivādaṃ nibodhata //
meaning:
ख्याप्यमानाम् अजातिं तैर् अनुमोदामहे वयम्
विवदामो न तैः सार्धम् अविवादं निबोधत //
text_mt: We approve the non-origination that is being proclaimed by them; / we do not dispute with them; understand non-disputation!

sanskrit_iast:
ajātasyaiva dharmasya jātim icchanti vādinaḥ
ajāto hy amṛto dharmo martyatāṃ katham eṣyati //
meaning:
अजातस्यैव धर्मस्य जातिम् इच्छन्ति वादिनः
अजातो ह्य् अमृतो धर्मो मर्त्यतां कथम् एष्यति //
text_mt: Disputants maintain the birth of an entity that is unborn; / for how could an entity, unborn and immortal, undergo mortality?

sanskrit_iast:
na bhavaty amṛtaṃ martyaṃ na martyam amṛtaṃ tathā
prakṛter anyathābhāvo na kathaṃcid bhaviṣyati //
meaning:
न भवत्य् अमृतं मर्त्यं न मर्त्यम् अमृतं तथा
प्रकृतेर् अन्यथाभावो न कथंचिद् भविष्यति //
text_mt: The immortal does not become mortal, nor does the mortal become immortal; / there will never be an alteration of inherent nature in any way.

sanskrit_iast:
svabhāvenāmṛto yasya dharmo gacchati martyatām
kṛtakenāmṛtas tasya kathaṃ sthāsyati niścalaḥ //
meaning:
स्वभावेनामृतो यस्य धर्मो गच्छति मर्त्यताम्
कृतकेनामृतस् तस्य कथं स्थास्यति निश्चलः //
text_mt: If one's entity is immortal by own-nature and undergoes mortality, / how will it, made immortal through an artificial condition, remain motionless?

sanskrit_iast:
sāṃsiddhikī svābhāvikī sahajā akṛtā ca yā
prakṛtiḥ seti vijñeyā svabhāvaṃ na jahāti yā //
meaning:
सांसिद्धिकी स्वाभाविकी सहजा अकृता च या
प्रकृतिः सेति विज्ञेया स्वभावं न जहाति या //
text_mt: That which is innate, natural, inborn, and unproduced, / and which does not abandon its own-nature, should be known as inherent nature.

sanskrit_iast:
jarāmaraṇanirmuktāḥ sarve dharmāḥ svabhāvataḥ
jarāmaraṇam icchantaś cyavante tanmanīṣayā //
meaning:
जरामरणनिर्मुक्ताः सर्वे धर्माः स्वभावतः
जरामरणम् इच्छन्तश् च्यवन्ते तन्मनीषया //
text_mt: All entities are by own-nature free from old age and death; / conceiving of old age and death, they fall away through that conception.

sanskrit_iast:
kāraṇaṃ yasya vai kāryaṃ kāraṇaṃ tasya jāyate
jāyamānaṃ katham ajaṃ bhinnaṃ nityaṃ kathaṃ ca tat //
meaning:
कारणं यस्य वै कार्यं कारणं तस्य जायते
जायमानं कथम् अजं भिन्नं नित्यं कथं च तत् //
text_mt: For him for whom the cause is indeed the effect, the cause is born; / being born, how is it unborn? And how is it eternal if diversified?

sanskrit_iast:
kāraṇād yady ananyatvam ataḥ kāryam ajaṃ tava
jāyamānād dhi vai kāryāt kāraṇaṃ te kathaṃ dhruvam //
meaning:
कारणाद् यद्य् अनन्यत्वम् अतः कार्यम् अजं तव
जायमानाद् धि वै कार्यात् कारणं ते कथं ध्रुवम् //
text_mt: If the effect is non-different from the cause, then your effect must be unborn; / and how could your cause be permanent, being identical to the effect that is being born?

sanskrit_iast:
ajād vai jāyate yasya dṛṣṭāntas tasya nāsti vai
jātāc ca jāyamānasya na vyavasthā prasajyate //
meaning:
अजाद् वै जायते यस्य दृष्टान्तस् तस्य नास्ति वै
जाताच् च जायमानस्य न व्यवस्था प्रसज्यते //
text_mt: For him who holds that it is born from the unborn, there is no example; / and for what is born from what is born, an infinite regress follows.

sanskrit_iast:
hetor ādiḥ phalaṃ yeṣām ādir hetuḥ phalasya ca
hetoḥ phalasya cānādiḥ kathaṃ tair upavarṇyate //
meaning:
हेतोर् आदिः फलं येषाम् आदिर् हेतुः फलस्य च
हेतोः फलस्य चानादिः कथं तैर् उपवर्ण्यते //
text_mt: For those for whom the fruit is the beginning of the cause, and the cause is the beginning of the fruit, / how is beginninglessness of cause and fruit described by them?

sanskrit_iast:
hetor ādiḥ phalaṃ yeṣām ādir hetuḥ phalasya ca
tathā janma bhavet teṣāṃ putrāj janma pitur yathā //
meaning:
हेतोर् आदिः फलं येषाम् आदिर् हेतुः फलस्य च
तथा जन्म भवेत् तेषां पुत्राज् जन्म पितुर् यथा //
text_mt: For those for whom the fruit is the beginning of the cause, and the cause is the beginning of the fruit, / their origination would be just like the birth of the father from the son.

sanskrit_iast:
saṃbhave hetuphalayor eṣitavyaḥ kramas tvayā
yugapat saṃbhave yasmād asaṃbandho viṣāṇavat //
meaning:
संभवे हेतुफलयोर् एषितव्यः क्रमस् त्वया
युगपत् संभवे यस्माद् असंबन्धो विषाणवत् //
text_mt: If cause and fruit are produced, an order must be postulated by you; / for if they arise simultaneously, there is no connection, like [the two] horns [of a cow].

sanskrit_iast:
phalād utpadyamānaḥ san na te hetuḥ prasidhyati
aprasiddhaḥ kathaṃ hetuḥ phalam utpādayiṣyati //
meaning:
फलाद् उत्पद्यमानः सन् न ते हेतुः प्रसिध्यति
अप्रसिद्धः कथं हेतुः फलम् उत्पादयिष्यति //
text_mt: Arising from the fruit, your cause cannot be established; / how will an unestablished cause bring about a fruit?

sanskrit_iast:
yadi hetoḥ phalāt siddhiḥ phalasiddhiś ca hetutaḥ
katarat pūrvaniṣpannaṃ yasya siddhir apekṣayā //
meaning:
यदि हेतोः फलात् सिद्धिः फलसिद्धिश् च हेतुतः
कतरत् पूर्वनिष्पन्नं यस्य सिद्धिर् अपेक्षया //
text_mt: If the cause is established from the fruit, and the establishment of the fruit is from the cause, / which of the two is produced first, when the establishment of either depends [on the other]?

sanskrit_iast:
aśaktir aparijñānaṃ kramakopo 'tha vā punaḥ
evaṃ hi sarvathā buddhair ajātiḥ paridīpitā //
meaning:
अशक्तिर् अपरिज्ञानं क्रमकोपो ऽथ वा पुनः
एवं हि सर्वथा बुद्धैर् अजातिः परिदीपिता //
text_mt: Inability [to answer], failure of comprehension, or indeed disruption of the order— / thus, in every way, non-origination is illuminated by the awakened.

sanskrit_iast:
bījāṅkurākhyo dṛṣṭāntaḥ sadā sādhyasamo hi saḥ
na hi sādhyasamo hetuḥ siddhau sādhyasya yujyate //
meaning:
बीजाङ्कुराख्यो दृष्टान्तः सदा साध्यसमो हि सः
न हि साध्यसमो हेतुः सिद्धौ साध्यस्य युज्यते //
text_mt: The example called 'seed and sprout' is indeed always equivalent to the probandum; / and a reason equivalent to the probandum is not fit for establishing the probandum.

sanskrit_iast:
pūrvāparāparijñānam ajāteḥ paridīpakam
jāyamānād dhi vai dharmāt kathaṃ pūrvaṃ na gṛhyate //
meaning:
पूर्वापरापरिज्ञानम् अजातेः परिदीपकम्
जायमानाद् धि वै धर्मात् कथं पूर्वं न गृह्यते //
text_mt: Failure to comprehend the prior and the posterior illuminates non-origination; / for how can the prior not be apprehended before the entity that is being born?

sanskrit_iast:
svato vā parato vāpi na kiṃcid vastu jāyate
sad asat sadasad vāpi na kiṃcid vastu jāyate //
meaning:
स्वतो वा परतो वापि न किंचिद् वस्तु जायते
सद् असत् सदसद् वापि न किंचिद् वस्तु जायते //
text_mt: Neither from itself nor from another is any real object born; / whether existent, non-existent, or both existent and non-existent, no real object is born.

sanskrit_iast:
hetur na jāyate anādeḥ phalaṃ cāpi svabhāvataḥ
ādir na vidyate yasya tasya hy ādir na vidyate //
meaning:
हेतुर् न जायते अनादेः फलं चापि स्वभावतः
आदिर् न विद्यते यस्य तस्य ह्य् आदिर् न विद्यते //
text_mt: A cause is not born, being beginningless; nor is a fruit, by its own-nature. / That which has no beginning has no origination.

sanskrit_iast:
prajñapteḥ sanimittatvam anyathā dvayanāśataḥ
saṃkleśasyopalabdheś ca paratantrāstitā matā //
meaning:
प्रज्ञप्तेः सनिमित्तत्वम् अन्यथा द्वयनाशतः
संक्लेशस्योपलब्धेश् च परतन्त्रास्तिता मता //
text_mt: Conventional designation must have a cause, otherwise there would be the destruction of duality; / and because affliction is perceived, the existence of the dependent [nature] is maintained.

sanskrit_iast:
prajñapteḥ sanimittatvam iṣyate yuktidarśanāt
nimittasyānimittatvam iṣyate bhūtadarśanāt //
meaning:
प्रज्ञप्तेः सनिमित्तत्वम् इष्यते युक्तिदर्शनात्
निमित्तस्यानिमित्तत्वम् इष्यते भूतदर्शनात् //
text_mt: Conventional designation having a cause is accepted from the perspective of reasoning; / that the cause has no cause is accepted from the perspective of reality.

sanskrit_iast:
cittaṃ na saṃspṛśaty arthaṃ nārthābhāsaṃ tathaiva ca
abhūto hi yataś cārtho nārthābhāsas tataḥ pṛthak //
meaning:
चित्तं न संस्पृशत्य् अर्थं नार्थाभासं तथैव च
अभूतो हि यतश् चार्थो नार्थाभासस् ततः पृथक् //
text_mt: The mind does not touch an object, nor indeed the appearance of an object; / for the object is non-existent, and the appearance of an object is not separate from it.

sanskrit_iast:
nimittaṃ na sadā cittaṃ saṃspṛśaty adhvasu triṣu
animitto viparyāsaḥ kathaṃ tasya bhaviṣyati //
meaning:
निमित्तं न सदा चित्तं संस्पृशत्य् अध्वसु त्रिषु
अनिमित्तो विपर्यासः कथं तस्य भविष्यति //
text_mt: The mind never touches a cause in the three times; / how will there be error without a cause?

sanskrit_iast:
tasmān na jāyate cittaṃ cittadṛśyaṃ na jāyate
tasya paśyanti ye jātiṃ khe vai paśyanti te padam //
meaning:
तस्मान् न जायते चित्तं चित्तदृश्यं न जायते
तस्य पश्यन्ति ये जातिं खे वै पश्यन्ति ते पदम् //
text_mt: Therefore the mind is not born, and what is seen by the mind is not born; / those who see its birth see a footprint in the sky.

sanskrit_iast:
ajātaṃ jāyate yasmād ajātiḥ prakṛtis tataḥ
prakṛter anyathābhāvo na kathaṃcid bhaviṣyati //
meaning:
अजातं जायते यस्माद् अजातिः प्रकृतिस् ततः
प्रकृतेर् अन्यथाभावो न कथंचिद् भविष्यति //
text_mt: Since that which is unborn is born, non-origination is therefore its inherent nature; / there can in no way be an alteration of inherent nature.

sanskrit_iast:
anāder antavattvaṃ ca saṃsārasya na setsyate
anantatā cādimato mokṣasya na bhaviṣyati //
meaning:
अनादेर् अन्तवत्त्वं च संसारस्य न सेत्स्यते
अनन्तता चादिमतो मोक्षस्य न भविष्यति //
text_mt: And the beginningless saṃsāra cannot be shown to have an end; / nor will liberation, which would have a beginning, be endless.

sanskrit_iast:
ādāv ante ca yan nāsti vartamāne 'pi tat tathā
vitathaiḥ sadṛśāḥ santo avitathā iva lakṣitāḥ //
meaning:
आदाव् अन्ते च यन् नास्ति वर्तमाने ऽपि तत् तथा
वितथैः सदृशाः सन्तो अवितथा इव लक्षिताः //
text_mt: That which does not exist in the beginning and at the end does not exist likewise in the present; / being similar to unreal things, they are perceived as if real.

sanskrit_iast:
saprayojanatā teṣāṃ svapne vipratipadyate
tasmād ādyantavattvena mithyaiva khalu te smṛtāḥ //
meaning:
सप्रयोजनता तेषां स्वप्ने विप्रतिपद्यते
तस्माद् आद्यन्तवत्त्वेन मिथ्यैव खलु ते स्मृताः //
text_mt: Their practical efficacy is contradicted in a dream; / therefore, because they have a beginning and an end, they are regarded as entirely false.

sanskrit_iast:
sarve dharmā mṛṣā svapne kāyasyāntarnidarśanāt
saṃvṛte 'smin pradeśe vai bhūtānāṃ darśanaṃ kutaḥ //
meaning:
सर्वे धर्मा मृषा स्वप्ने कायस्यान्तर्निदर्शनात्
संवृते ऽस्मिन् प्रदेशे वै भूतानां दर्शनं कुतः //
text_mt: All entities in a dream are false, because they are seen within the body; / within this enclosed space, whence could there be the seeing of actual things?

sanskrit_iast:
na yuktaṃ darśanaṃ gatvā kālasyāniyamād gatau
pratibuddhaś ca vai sarvas tasmin deśe na vidyate //
meaning:
न युक्तं दर्शनं गत्वा कालस्यानियमाद् गतौ
प्रतिबुद्धश् च वै सर्वस् तस्मिन् देशे न विद्यते //
text_mt: It is not plausible that [the dreamer] sees after going [there], because of the inadequacy of time for going; / and on waking up, no one is in that place.

sanskrit_iast:
mitrādyaiḥ saha saṃmantrya saṃbuddho na prapadyate
gṛhītaṃ cāpi yat kiṃcit pratibuddho na paśyati //
meaning:
मित्राद्यैः सह संमन्त्र्य संबुद्धो न प्रपद्यते
गृहीतं चापि यत् किंचित् प्रतिबुद्धो न पश्यति //
text_mt: Conferring with friends and others, he does not reach [them] upon waking; / and whatever he grasped, upon waking he does not see.

sanskrit_iast:
svapne cāvastukaḥ kāyaḥ pṛthag anyasya darśanāt
yathā kāyas tathā sarvaṃ cittadṛśyam avastukam //
meaning:
स्वप्ने चावस्तुकः कायः पृथग् अन्यस्य दर्शनात्
यथा कायस् तथा सर्वं चित्तदृश्यम् अवस्तुकम् //
text_mt: And in a dream the body is a non-object, because another is seen separate [from it]; / as the body is, so everything seen by the mind is a non-object.

sanskrit_iast:
grahaṇāj jāgaritavat taddhetuḥ svapne iṣyate
taddhetutvāt tu tasyaiva saj jāgaritam iṣyate //
meaning:
ग्रहणाज् जागरितवत् तद्धेतुः स्वप्ने इष्यते
तद्धेतुत्वात् तु तस्यैव सज् जागरितम् इष्यते //
text_mt: Because of apprehension, the dream is held to have that [waking state] as its cause, like the waking state; / and because it is the cause of that, the waking state alone is held to be real.

sanskrit_iast:
utpādasyāprasiddhatvād ajaṃ sarvam udāhṛtam
na ca bhūtād abhūtasya saṃbhavo 'sti kathaṃcana //
meaning:
उत्पादस्याप्रसिद्धत्वाद् अजं सर्वम् उदाहृतम्
न च भूताद् अभूतस्य संभवो ऽस्ति कथंचन //
text_mt: Because origination is unestablished, everything is declared unborn; / and in no way can the non-existent arise from the existent.

sanskrit_iast:
asaj jāgarite dṛṣṭvā svapne paśyati tanmayaḥ
asat svapne 'pi dṛṣṭvā ca pratibuddho na paśyati //
meaning:
असज् जागरिते दृष्ट्वा स्वप्ने पश्यति तन्मयः
असत् स्वप्ने ऽपि दृष्ट्वा च प्रतिबुद्धो न पश्यति //
text_mt: Having seen the unreal in the waking state, he sees it in a dream, absorbed in it; / and having seen the unreal even in a dream, he does not see it upon waking.

sanskrit_iast:
nāsty asaddhetukam asat sad asaddhetukaṃ tathā
sac ca saddhetukaṃ nāsti saddhetukam asat kutaḥ //
meaning:
नास्त्य् असद्धेतुकम् असत् सद् असद्धेतुकं तथा
सच् च सद्धेतुकं नास्ति सद्धेतुकम् असत् कुतः //
text_mt: The non-existent cannot have the non-existent as its cause, nor the existent have the non-existent as its cause; / and the existent cannot have the existent as its cause—how could the non-existent have the existent as its cause?

sanskrit_iast:
viparyāsād yathā jāgrad acintyān bhūtavat spṛśet
tathā svapne viparyāsād dharmāṃs tatraiva paśyati //
meaning:
विपर्यासाद् यथा जाग्रद् अचिन्त्यान् भूतवत् स्पृशेत्
तथा स्वप्ने विपर्यासाद् धर्मांस् तत्रैव पश्यति //
text_mt: Just as the waking person, through error, touches inconceivable things as if real, / so in a dream, through error, he sees entities right there.

sanskrit_iast:
upalambhāt samācārād astivastutvavādinām
jātis tu deśitā buddhair ajātes trasatāṃ sadā //
meaning:
उपलम्भात् समाचाराद् अस्तिवस्तुत्ववादिनाम्
जातिस् तु देशिता बुद्धैर् अजातेस् त्रसतां सदा //
text_mt: Origination was taught by the awakened on account of perceptual apprehension and customary practice / to those who profess the reality of real objects and are ever terrified of non-origination.

sanskrit_iast:
ajātes trasatāṃ teṣām upalaṃbhād viyanti ye
jātidoṣā na setsyanti doṣo 'py alpo bhaviṣyati //
meaning:
अजातेस् त्रसतां तेषाम् उपलंभाद् वियन्ति ये
जातिदोषा न सेत्स्यन्ति दोषो ऽप्य् अल्पो भविष्यति //
text_mt: For those who are terrified of non-origination and deviate [from the truth] due to perceptual apprehension, / the flaws of origination will not hold; their fault will even be slight.

sanskrit_iast:
upalambhāt samācārān māyāhastī yathocyate
upalambhāt samācārād asti vastu tathocyate //
meaning:
उपलम्भात् समाचारान् मायाहस्ती यथोच्यते
उपलम्भात् समाचाराद् अस्ति वस्तु तथोच्यते //
text_mt: Just as an elephant of illusion is spoken of on account of perceptual apprehension and customary practice, / so a real object is said to exist on account of perceptual apprehension and customary practice.

sanskrit_iast:
jātyābhāsaṃ calābhāsaṃ vastvābhāsaṃ tathaiva ca
ajācalam avastutvaṃ vijñānaṃ śāntam advayam //
meaning:
जात्याभासं चलाभासं वस्त्वाभासं तथैव च
अजाचलम् अवस्तुत्वं विज्ञानं शान्तम् अद्वयम् //
text_mt: Having the appearance of birth, the appearance of motion, and likewise the appearance of a real object, / consciousness is unborn, motionless, a non-object, tranquil, and non-dual.

sanskrit_iast:
evaṃ na jāyate cittam evaṃ dharmā ajāḥ smṛtāḥ
evam eva vijānanto na patanti viparyaye //
meaning:
एवं न जायते चित्तम् एवं धर्मा अजाः स्मृताः
एवम् एव विजानन्तो न पतन्ति विपर्यये //
text_mt: Thus the mind is not born; thus entities are held to be unborn; / knowing in this very way, they do not fall into error.

sanskrit_iast:
ṛjuvakrādikābhāsam alātaspanditaṃ yathā
grahaṇagrāhakābhāsaṃ vijñānaspanditaṃ tathā //
meaning:
ऋजुवक्रादिकाभासम् अलातस्पन्दितं यथा
ग्रहणग्राहकाभासं विज्ञानस्पन्दितं तथा //
text_mt: Just as a whirling firebrand appears straight, crooked, and so on, / so the vibration of consciousness appears as the grasped and the grasper.

sanskrit_iast:
aspandamānam alātam anābhāsam ajaṃ yathā
aspandamānaṃ vijñānam anābhāsam ajaṃ tathā //
meaning:
अस्पन्दमानम् अलातम् अनाभासम् अजं यथा
अस्पन्दमानं विज्ञानम् अनाभासम् अजं तथा //
text_mt: Just as an unwhirled firebrand is without appearance and unborn, / so unvibrating consciousness is without appearance and unborn.

sanskrit_iast:
alāte spandamāne vai nābhāsā anyatobhuvaḥ
na tato 'nyatra nispandān nālātaṃ praviśanti te //
meaning:
अलाते स्पन्दमाने वै नाभासा अन्यतोभुवः
न ततो ऽन्यत्र निस्पन्दान् नालातं प्रविशन्ति ते //
text_mt: When the firebrand is whirled, the appearances do not come from elsewhere; / motionless, they do not go anywhere other than that, nor do they enter the firebrand.

sanskrit_iast:
na nirgatā alātāt te dravyatvābhāvayogataḥ
vijñāne 'pi tathaiva syur ābhāsasyāviśeṣataḥ //
meaning:
न निर्गता अलातात् ते द्रव्यत्वाभावयोगतः
विज्ञाने ऽपि तथैव स्युर् आभासस्याविशेषतः //
text_mt: They have not issued from the firebrand, because they lack substantiality; / the same must be true of consciousness, because the appearance is identical.

sanskrit_iast:
vijñāne spandamāne vai nābhāsā anyatobhuvaḥ
na tato 'nyatra nispandān na vijñānaṃ viśanti te //
meaning:
विज्ञाने स्पन्दमाने वै नाभासा अन्यतोभुवः
न ततो ऽन्यत्र निस्पन्दान् न विज्ञानं विशन्ति ते //
text_mt: When consciousness vibrates, the appearances do not come from elsewhere; / motionless, they do not go anywhere other than that, nor do they enter consciousness.

sanskrit_iast:
na nirgatās te vijñānād dravyatvābhāvayogataḥ
kāryakāraṇatābhāvād yato 'cintyāḥ sadaiva te //
meaning:
न निर्गतास् ते विज्ञानाद् द्रव्यत्वाभावयोगतः
कार्यकारणताभावाद् यतो ऽचिन्त्याः सदैव ते //
text_mt: They have not issued from consciousness, because they lack substantiality, / since they are ever inconceivable due to the absence of causality.

sanskrit_iast:
dravyaṃ dravyasya hetuḥ syād anyad anyasya caiva hi
dravyatvam anyabhāvo vā dharmāṇāṃ nopapadyate //
meaning:
द्रव्यं द्रव्यस्य हेतुः स्याद् अन्यद् अन्यस्य चैव हि
द्रव्यत्वम् अन्यभावो वा धर्माणां नोपपद्यते //
text_mt: A substance might be the cause of a substance, and another of another; / but neither substantiality nor otherness is possible for entities.

sanskrit_iast:
evaṃ na cittajā dharmāś cittaṃ vāpi na dharmajam
evaṃ hetuphalājātiṃ praviśanti manīṣiṇaḥ //
meaning:
एवं न चित्तजा धर्माश् चित्तं वापि न धर्मजम्
एवं हेतुफलाजातिं प्रविशन्ति मनीषिणः //
text_mt: Thus entities are not born from the mind, nor is the mind born from entities; / thus the wise enter into the non-origination of cause and fruit.

sanskrit_iast:
yāvad dhetuphalāveśas tāvad dhetuphalodbhavaḥ
kṣīṇe hetuphalāveśe nāsti hetuphalodbhavaḥ //
meaning:
यावद् धेतुफलावेशस् तावद् धेतुफलोद्भवः
क्षीणे हेतुफलावेशे नास्ति हेतुफलोद्भवः //
text_mt: As long as there is obsession with cause and fruit, so long is there the arising of cause and fruit; / when obsession with cause and fruit is exhausted, there is no arising of cause and fruit.

sanskrit_iast:
yāvad dhetuphalāveśaḥ saṃsāras tāvad āyataḥ
kṣīṇe hetuphalāveśe saṃsāraṃ na prapadyate //
meaning:
यावद् धेतुफलावेशः संसारस् तावद् आयतः
क्षीणे हेतुफलावेशे संसारं न प्रपद्यते //
text_mt: As long as there is obsession with cause and fruit, so long is saṃsāra extended; / when obsession with cause and fruit is exhausted, one does not undergo saṃsāra.

sanskrit_iast:
saṃvṛtyā jāyate sarvaṃ śāśvataṃ nāsti tena vai
sadbhāvena hy ajaṃ sarvam ucchedas tena nāsti vai //
meaning:
संवृत्या जायते सर्वं शाश्वतं नास्ति तेन वै
सद्भावेन ह्य् अजं सर्वम् उच्छेदस् तेन नास्ति वै //
text_mt: Everything is born through concealment; therefore nothing is eternal; / everything is unborn by its own nature; therefore there is no annihilation.

sanskrit_iast:
dharmā ye iti jāyante jāyante te na tattvataḥ
janma māyopamaṃ teṣāṃ sā ca māyā na vidyate //
meaning:
धर्मा ये इति जायन्ते जायन्ते ते न तत्त्वतः
जन्म मायोपमं तेषां सा च माया न विद्यते //
text_mt: Those entities that are said to be born are born through concealment, not in reality; / their birth is like an illusion, and that illusion does not exist.

sanskrit_iast:
yathā māyāmayād bījāj jāyate tanmayo 'ṅkuraḥ
nāsau nityo na cocchedī tadvad dharmeṣu yojanā //
meaning:
यथा मायामयाद् बीजाज् जायते तन्मयो ऽङ्कुरः
नासौ नित्यो न चोच्छेदी तद्वद् धर्मेषु योजना //
text_mt: Just as from an illusory seed is born a sprout of the same nature, / which is neither eternal nor destructible, so is the application to entities.

sanskrit_iast:
nājeṣu sarvadharmeṣu śāśvatāśāśvatābhidhā
yatra varṇā na vartante vivekas tatra nocyate //
meaning:
नाजेषु सर्वधर्मेषु शाश्वताशाश्वताभिधा
यत्र वर्णा न वर्तन्ते विवेकस् तत्र नोच्यते //
text_mt: Among all unborn entities, the designation 'eternal' or 'non-eternal' does not apply; / where syllables do not function, no distinction is expressed there.

sanskrit_iast:
yathā svapne dvayābhāsaṃ cittaṃ calati māyayā
tathā jāgrad dvayābhāsaṃ cittaṃ calati māyayā //
meaning:
यथा स्वप्ने द्वयाभासं चित्तं चलति मायया
तथा जाग्रद् द्वयाभासं चित्तं चलति मायया //
text_mt: Just as in a dream the mind moves by illusion with the appearance of duality, / so in the waking state the mind moves by illusion with the appearance of duality.

sanskrit_iast:
advayaṃ ca dvayābhāsaṃ cittaṃ svapne na saṃśayaḥ
advayaṃ ca dvayābhāsaṃ tathā jāgran na saṃśayaḥ //
meaning:
अद्वयं च द्वयाभासं चित्तं स्वप्ने न संशयः
अद्वयं च द्वयाभासं तथा जाग्रन् न संशयः //
text_mt: And the mind, though non-dual, appears as dual in a dream, without doubt; / and the mind, though non-dual, appears as dual in the waking state, without doubt.

sanskrit_iast:
svapnadṛk pracaran svapne dikṣu vai daśasu sthitān
aṇḍajān svedajān vāpi jīvān paśyati yān sadā //
meaning:
स्वप्नदृक् प्रचरन् स्वप्ने दिक्षु वै दशसु स्थितान्
अण्डजान् स्वेदजान् वापि जीवान् पश्यति यान् सदा //
text_mt:
The dreamer moving about in dream sees individual souls
abiding in the ten directions, whether born from eggs or sweat.

sanskrit_iast:
svapnadṛkcittadṛśyās te na vidyante tataḥ pṛthak
tathā taddṛśyam evedaṃ svapnadṛkcittam iṣyate //
meaning:
स्वप्नदृक्चित्तदृश्यास् ते न विद्यन्ते ततः पृथक्
तथा तद्दृश्यम् एवेदं स्वप्नदृक्चित्तम् इष्यते //
text_mt:
Being perceived by the mind of the dreamer, they do not exist apart from it;
likewise, this mind of the dreamer is held to be only that which is perceived by it.

sanskrit_iast:
carañ jāgarite jāgrad dikṣu vai daśasu sthitān
aṇḍajān svedajān vāpi jīvān paśyati yān sadā //
meaning:
चरञ् जागरिते जाग्रद् दिक्षु वै दशसु स्थितान्
अण्डजान् स्वेदजान् वापि जीवान् पश्यति यान् सदा //
text_mt:
The waking person moving about in the waking state sees individual souls
abiding in the ten directions, whether born from eggs or sweat.

sanskrit_iast:
jāgraccittekṣaṇīyās te na vidyante tataḥ pṛthak
tathā taddṛśyam evedaṃ jāgrataś cittam iṣyate //
meaning:
जाग्रच्चित्तेक्षणीयास् ते न विद्यन्ते ततः पृथक्
तथा तद्दृश्यम् एवेदं जाग्रतश् चित्तम् इष्यते //
text_mt:
Being perceived by the mind of the waking person, they do not exist apart from it;
likewise, this mind of the waking person is held to be only that which is perceived by it.

sanskrit_iast:
ubhe hy anyoanyadṛśye te kiṃ tad astīti cocyate
lakṣaṇāśūnyam ubhayaṃ tanmatenaiva gṛhyate //
meaning:
उभे ह्य् अन्योअन्यदृश्ये ते किं तद् अस्तीति चोच्यते
लक्षणाशून्यम् उभयं तन्मतेनैव गृह्यते //
text_mt:
Indeed, both are mutually perceived; what is it that is said to exist?
Both are devoid of characteristics; each is grasped only by thought of the other.

sanskrit_iast:
yathā svapnamayo jīvo jāyate mriyate 'pi ca
tathā jīvā amī sarve bhavanti na bhavanti ca //
meaning:
यथा स्वप्नमयो जीवो जायते म्रियते ऽपि च
तथा जीवा अमी सर्वे भवन्ति न भवन्ति च //
text_mt:
Just as an individual soul composed of dream is born and dies,
so all these individual souls exist and cease to exist.

sanskrit_iast:
yathā māyāmayo jīvo jāyate mriyate 'pi ca
tathā jīvā amī sarve bhavanti na bhavanti ca //
meaning:
यथा मायामयो जीवो जायते म्रियते ऽपि च
तथा जीवा अमी सर्वे भवन्ति न भवन्ति च //
text_mt:
Just as an individual soul composed of illusion is born and dies,
so all these individual souls exist and cease to exist.

sanskrit_iast:
yathā nirmitako jīvo jāyate mriyate 'pi ca
tathā jīvā amī sarve bhavanti na bhavanti ca //
meaning:
यथा निर्मितको जीवो जायते म्रियते ऽपि च
तथा जीवा अमी सर्वे भवन्ति न भवन्ति च //
text_mt:
Just as an individual soul artificially created is born and dies,
so all these individual souls exist and cease to exist.

sanskrit_iast:
na kaścij jāyate jīvaḥ saṃbhavo 'sya na vidyate
etat tad uttamaṃ satyaṃ yatra kiṃcin na jāyate //
meaning:
न कश्चिज् जायते जीवः संभवो ऽस्य न विद्यते
एतत् तद् उत्तमं सत्यं यत्र किंचिन् न जायते //
text_mt:
No individual soul is ever born; no origination exists for it.
This is the supreme truth: where nothing whatsoever is born.

sanskrit_iast:
cittaspanditam evedaṃ grāhyagrāhakavad dvayam
cittaṃ nirviṣayaṃ nityam asaṅgaṃ tena kīrtitam //
meaning:
चित्तस्पन्दितम् एवेदं ग्राह्यग्राहकवद् द्वयम्
चित्तं निर्विषयं नित्यम् असङ्गं तेन कीर्तितम् //
text_mt:
This duality, appearing as grasped and grasper, is merely the vibration of the mind.
The mind is eternally devoid of objects; therefore it is proclaimed to be unattached.

sanskrit_iast:
yo 'sti kalpitasaṃvṛtyā paramārthena nāsty asau
paratantrābhisaṃvṛtyā syān nāsti paramārthataḥ //
meaning:
यो ऽस्ति कल्पितसंवृत्या परमार्थेन नास्त्य् असौ
परतन्त्राभिसंवृत्या स्यान् नास्ति परमार्थतः //
text_mt:
That which exists by conceptual concealment does not exist in ultimate truth;
that which exists by dependent concealment does not exist in ultimate truth.

sanskrit_iast:
ajaḥ kalpitasaṃvṛtyā paramārthena nāpy ajaḥ
paratantrābhiniṣpattyā saṃvṛtyā jāyate tu saḥ //
meaning:
अजः कल्पितसंवृत्या परमार्थेन नाप्य् अजः
परतन्त्राभिनिष्पत्त्या संवृत्या जायते तु सः //
text_mt:
It is unborn by conceptual concealment, and in ultimate truth it is not even unborn;
yet through dependent production it is born by concealment.

sanskrit_iast:
abhūtābhiniveśo 'sti dvayaṃ tatra na vidyate
dvayābhāvaṃ sa buddhvaiva nirnimitto na jāyate //
meaning:
अभूताभिनिवेशो ऽस्ति द्वयं तत्र न विद्यते
द्वयाभावं स बुद्ध्वैव निर्निमित्तो न जायते //
text_mt:
There is adherence to the unreal, [yet] no duality exists there;
having awakened to the non-existence of duality, causeless, one is not born.

sanskrit_iast:
yadā na labhate hetūn uttamādhamamadhyamān
tadā na jāyate cittaṃ hetvabhāve phalaṃ kutaḥ //
meaning:
यदा न लभते हेतून् उत्तमाधममध्यमान्
तदा न जायते चित्तं हेत्वभावे फलं कुतः //
text_mt:
When the mind does not obtain causes—higher, lower, or middle—
then it is not born. In the absence of a cause, whence the fruit?

sanskrit_iast:
animittasya cittasya yānutpattiḥ samādvayā
ajātasyaiva sarvasya cittadṛśyaṃ hi tad yataḥ //
meaning:
अनिमित्तस्य चित्तस्य यानुत्पत्तिः समाद्वया
अजातस्यैव सर्वस्य चित्तदृश्यं हि तद् यतः //
text_mt:
The non-origination of the causeless mind is equal and non-dual,
for all of it is indeed unborn, since it is an object perceived by the mind.

sanskrit_iast:
buddhvānimittatāṃ satyāṃ hetuṃ pṛthag anāpnuvan
vītaśokaṃ tathākāmam abhayaṃ padam aśnute //
meaning:
बुद्ध्वानिमित्ततां सत्यां हेतुं पृथग् अनाप्नुवन्
वीतशोकं तथाकामम् अभयं पदम् अश्नुते //
text_mt:
Awakening to true causelessness, not finding a separate cause,
one attains the sorrowless, desireless, and fearless state.

sanskrit_iast:
abhūtābhiniveśād dhi sadṛśe tat pravartate
vastvabhāvaṃ sa buddhvaiva niḥsaṅgaṃ vinivartate //
meaning:
अभूताभिनिवेशाद् धि सदृशे तत् प्रवर्तते
वस्त्वभावं स बुद्ध्वैव निःसङ्गं विनिवर्तते //
text_mt:
Due to adherence to the unreal, it proceeds towards what resembles it;
having awakened to the non-existence of real objects, unattached, it turns back.

sanskrit_iast:
nivṛttasyāpravṛttasya niścalā hi tadā sthitiḥ
viṣayaḥ sa hi buddhānāṃ tat sāmyam ajam advayam //
meaning:
निवृत्तस्याप्रवृत्तस्य निश्चला हि तदा स्थितिः
विषयः स हि बुद्धानां तत् साम्यम् अजम् अद्वयम् //
text_mt:
When it has turned back and does not proceed, its state is then unwavering;
for that is the sphere of the awakened: that sameness, unborn and non-dual.

sanskrit_iast:
ajam anidram asvapnaṃ prabhātaṃ bhavati svayam
sakṛdvibhāto hy evaiṣa dharmo dhātusvabhāvataḥ //
meaning:
अजम् अनिद्रम् अस्वप्नं प्रभातं भवति स्वयम्
सकृद्विभातो ह्य् एवैष धर्मो धातुस्वभावतः //
text_mt:
Unborn, sleepless, dreamless, it is self-illuminated;
for this entity is once and for all radiant by the own-nature of its element.

sanskrit_iast:
sukham āvriyate nityaṃ duḥkhaṃ vivriyate sadā
yasya kasya ca dharmasya graheṇa bhagavān asau //
meaning:
सुखम् आव्रियते नित्यं दुःखं विव्रियते सदा
यस्य कस्य च धर्मस्य ग्रहेण भगवान् असौ //
text_mt:
Happiness is eternally concealed and suffering is always exposed
by grasping any entity whatsoever, [though it is] the Lord.

sanskrit_iast:
asti nāsty asti nāstīti nāsti nāstīti vā punaḥ
calasthirobhayābhāvair āvṛṇoty eva bāliśaḥ //
meaning:
अस्ति नास्त्य् अस्ति नास्तीति नास्ति नास्तीति वा पुनः
चलस्थिरोभयाभावैर् आवृणोत्य् एव बालिशः //
text_mt:
‘It exists,’ ‘it does not exist,’ ‘it exists and does not exist,’ or again, ‘it does not exist, does not exist’—
with [notions of] change, stillness, both, and neither, the childish fool conceals [it].

sanskrit_iast:
koṭyaś catasra etās tu grahair yāsāṃ sadāvṛtaḥ
bhagavān ābhir aspṛṣṭo yena dṛṣṭaḥ sa sarvadṛk //
meaning:
कोट्यश् चतस्र एतास् तु ग्रहैर् यासां सदावृतः
भगवान् आभिर् अस्पृष्टो येन दृष्टः स सर्वदृक् //
text_mt:
These are the four extremes, by whose grasps [the Lord] is always concealed;
he who has seen the Lord untouched by these is all-seeing.

sanskrit_iast:
prāpya sarvajñatāṃ kṛtsnāṃ brāhmaṇyaṃ padam advayam
anāpannādimadhyāntaṃ kim ataḥ param īhate //
meaning:
प्राप्य सर्वज्ञतां कृत्स्नां ब्राह्मण्यं पदम् अद्वयम्
अनापन्नादिमध्यान्तं किम् अतः परम् ईहते //
text_mt:
Having attained complete omniscience, the state of the knower of Brahman, non-dual,
without beginning, middle, or end—what could one desire beyond this?

sanskrit_iast:
viprāṇāṃ vinayo hy eṣa śamaḥ prākṛta ucyate
damaḥ prakṛtidāntatvād evaṃ vidvāñ śamaṃ vrajet //
meaning:
विप्राणां विनयो ह्य् एष शमः प्राकृत उच्यते
दमः प्रकृतिदान्तत्वाद् एवं विद्वाञ् शमं व्रजेत् //
text_mt:
This is the humility of the wise; peace is said to be innate [to them];
self-control [is theirs] because they are naturally tamed. Knowing thus, the wise enters peace.

sanskrit_iast:
savastu sopalambhaṃ ca dvayaṃ laukikam iṣyate
avastu sopalambhaṃ ca śuddhaṃ laukikam iṣyate //
meaning:
सवस्तु सोपलम्भं च द्वयं लौकिकम् इष्यते
अवस्तु सोपलम्भं च शुद्धं लौकिकम् इष्यते //
text_mt:
Duality with real objects and perceptual apprehension is held to be worldly;
duality without real objects, [yet] with perceptual apprehension, is held to be purified worldly.

sanskrit_iast:
avastv anupalambhaṃ ca lokottaram iti smṛtam
jñānaṃ jñeyaṃ ca vijñeyaṃ sadā buddhaiḥ prakīrtitam //
meaning:
अवस्त्व् अनुपलम्भं च लोकोत्तरम् इति स्मृतम्
ज्ञानं ज्ञेयं च विज्ञेयं सदा बुद्धैः प्रकीर्तितम् //
text_mt:
Devoid of real objects and devoid of perceptual apprehension is remembered as transmundane;
knowledge and the knowable are to be understood, [as] always proclaimed by the awakened.

sanskrit_iast:
jñāne ca trividhe jñeye krameṇa vidite svayam
sarvajñatā hi sarvatra bhavatīha mahādhiyaḥ //
meaning:
ज्ञाने च त्रिविधे ज्ञेये क्रमेण विदिते स्वयम्
सर्वज्ञता हि सर्वत्र भवतीह महाधियः //
text_mt:
When the three kinds of knowledge and the knowable are known by oneself in succession,
then omniscience arises everywhere here for the one of great intellect.

sanskrit_iast:
heyajñeyāpyapākyāni vijñeyāny agrayāṇataḥ
teṣām anyatra vijñeyād upalambhas triṣu smṛtaḥ //
meaning:
हेयज्ञेयाप्यपाक्यानि विज्ञेयान्य् अग्रयाणतः
तेषाम् अन्यत्र विज्ञेयाद् उपलम्भस् त्रिषु स्मृतः //
text_mt:
What is to be abandoned, known, attained, and matured are to be understood from the highest vehicle;
among these, perceptual apprehension is remembered to belong to the three, apart from the knowable.

sanskrit_iast:
prakṛtyākāśavaj jñeyāḥ sarve dharmā anādayaḥ
vidyate na hi nānātvaṃ teṣāṃ kvacana kiṃcana //
meaning:
प्रकृत्याकाशवज् ज्ञेयाः सर्वे धर्मा अनादयः
विद्यते न हि नानात्वं तेषां क्वचन किंचन //
text_mt:
By inherent nature, like space, all entities should be known as beginningless;
no diversity whatsoever exists anywhere among them.

sanskrit_iast:
ādibuddhāḥ prakṛtyaiva sarve dharmāḥ suniścitāḥ
yasyaivaṃ bhavati kṣāntiḥ so 'mṛtatvāya kalpate //
meaning:
आदिबुद्धाः प्रकृत्यैव सर्वे धर्माः सुनिश्चिताः
यस्यैवं भवति क्षान्तिः सो ऽमृतत्वाय कल्पते //
text_mt:
All entities are primordially awakened, well-ascertained by inherent nature itself;
he who has such receptive acquiescence is fit for immortality.

sanskrit_iast:
ādiśāntā hy anutpannāḥ prakṛtyaiva sunirvṛtāḥ
sarve dharmāḥ samābhinnā ajaṃ sāmyaṃ viśāradam //
meaning:
आदिशान्ता ह्य् अनुत्पन्नाः प्रकृत्यैव सुनिर्वृताः
सर्वे धर्माः समाभिन्ना अजं साम्यं विशारदम् //
text_mt:
Primordially tranquil, unoriginated, entirely extinguished by inherent nature itself,
all entities are equal and non-different: unborn, pure sameness.

sanskrit_iast:
vaiśāradyaṃ tu vai nāsti bhede vicaratāṃ sadā
bhedanimnāḥ pṛthagvādās tasmāt te kṛpaṇāḥ smṛtāḥ //
meaning:
वैशारद्यं तु वै नास्ति भेदे विचरतां सदा
भेदनिम्नाः पृथग्वादास् तस्मात् ते कृपणाः स्मृताः //
text_mt:
There is indeed no clarity for those who always wander in difference;
those who assert difference are bent on difference; therefore they are remembered as wretched.

sanskrit_iast:
aje sāmye tu ye kecid bhaviṣyanti suniścitāḥ
te hi loke mahājñānās tac ca loko na gāhate //
meaning:
अजे साम्ये तु ये केचिद् भविष्यन्ति सुनिश्चिताः
ते हि लोके महाज्ञानास् तच् च लोको न गाहते //
text_mt:
Those who will be firmly resolved in unborn sameness
are indeed possessors of great knowledge in the world, and the world cannot plumb it.

sanskrit_iast:
ajeṣv ajam asaṃkrāntaṃ dharmeṣu jñānam iṣyate
yato na kramate jñānam asaṅgaṃ tena kīrtitam //
meaning:
अजेष्व् अजम् असंक्रान्तं धर्मेषु ज्ञानम् इष्यते
यतो न क्रमते ज्ञानम् असङ्गं तेन कीर्तितम् //
text_mt:
Knowledge is held to be unborn and not transitioned into unborn entities;
because knowledge does not move [into objects], it is proclaimed to be unattached.

sanskrit_iast:
aṇumātre 'pi vaidharmye jāyamāne 'vipaścitaḥ
asaṅgatā sadā nāsti kim utāvaraṇacyutiḥ //
meaning:
अणुमात्रे ऽपि वैधर्म्ये जायमाने ऽविपश्चितः
असङ्गता सदा नास्ति किम् उतावरणच्युतिः //
text_mt:
If difference even to an atomic degree is assumed by the unwise,
unattachment never exists; how much less the shedding of obscuration?

sanskrit_iast:
alabdhāvaraṇāḥ sarve dharmāḥ prakṛtinirmalāḥ
ādau buddhās tathā muktā budhyante iti nāyakāḥ //
meaning:
अलब्धावरणाः सर्वे धर्माः प्रकृतिनिर्मलाः
आदौ बुद्धास् तथा मुक्ता बुध्यन्ते इति नायकाः //
text_mt:
All entities have never acquired obscuration; they are pure by inherent nature,
awakened from the beginning, and likewise liberated—thus they are known, the masters.

sanskrit_iast:
kramate na hi buddhasya jñānaṃ dharmeṣu (tāpinaḥ ([B,K:]tāyinaḥ)
sarve dharmās tathā jñānaṃ naitad buddhena bhāṣitam //
meaning:
क्रमते न हि बुद्धस्य ज्ञानं धर्मेषु (तापिनः ([ब्,क्:]तायिनः)
सर्वे धर्मास् तथा ज्ञानं नैतद् बुद्धेन भाषितम् //
text_mt:
The knowledge of the awakened, the protector, does not pass into entities;
all entities likewise [do not pass into] knowledge: this was not spoken by the Buddha.

sanskrit_iast:
durdarśam atigambhīram ajaṃ sāmyaṃ viśāradam
buddhvā padam anānātvaṃ namas kurmo yathābalam //
meaning:
दुर्दर्शम् अतिगम्भीरम् अजं साम्यं विशारदम्
बुद्ध्वा पदम् अनानात्वं नमस् कुर्मो यथाबलम् //
text_mt:
Having awakened to the state hard to see, very deep, unborn, sameness, pure,
free from diversity, we pay homage to the best of our ability.
